name: Phantasmal Fireball
description: A manga panel of a hand holding a round object wrapped in flame, with a seal drawn on it, fully visible and ring closed. A large triangle is inscribed in the ring. At the center sits a fire sigil variant: a small triangle with three lines running outward from it, each ending in a filled square. Three branching, feather-like signs sit between the triangle's sides and the ring, at the north, east, and southwest, each pointing inward. Short pairs of parallel dashes sit in the remaining gaps between them. Outside the ring, three small looped marks with filled dots are attached by short lines at the west, northeast, and south. None of the surrounding signs match a named sign. The flame shading lies over the seal, but the lines remain legible.
justification: The central fire sigil variant sets the element as fire, and the square-ended lines set it apart from the plain fire sigil. The inscribed triangle and the three-fold arrangement of branching signs, dash pairs, and outer marks repeat evenly around the ring. That points to a balanced, centered manifestation rather than one aimed in a single direction. The individual effects of these unnamed signs cannot be decoded from shape alone, so the spell's behavior rests on the sigil variant.
effect: Forms an artificial flame that looks and acts like real fire and gives off light, but produces no heat. It can be touched without injury, still scares off beasts, and needs no fuel, so it never goes out.

name: Phantasmal Fireball
description: A manga panel with a fully visible seal, ring closed, set against grey textured shading. A large triangle is inscribed in the ring, with a small filled square at each of its three corners. At the center sits a small triangle crossed by a horizontal bar. It looks like a fire sigil with a crossbar and is close in shape to the Strengthening sign. Three identical branching signs sit just outside the triangle's edges, at the north, southwest and southeast. Each is a vertical stroke with angled side strokes, and none matches a known sign. Three small round knobs sit on the outer edge of the ring, at the northwest, northeast and south, lined up with the triangle's corners. Some fine strokes are soft at this resolution.
justification: The central triangle with its crossbar is a variant of the fire sigil, Unburning Flames. It places the spell in the domain of fire but changes what kind of flame is made. The inscribed triangle, corner squares, branching signs and ring knobs are modifiers outside the standard set, so their individual effects cannot be read from the sign rules. Their three-fold symmetry around the sigil points to an evenly shaped, contained flame rather than a directed one.
effect: Forms an artificial flame that looks and behaves like real fire and still gives off light, but produces no heat. It can be touched or held without any risk of burns, needs no fuel, and does not go out.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A manga panel of two hands holding up a tied cloth pouch with a diamond-shaped patch sewn on its front. A small circular seal is drawn on the patch, fully visible and ring closed, with a small dot on the ring at the north and south points. At the center is a Calling sigil: a small diamond flanked by two long curved strokes that bow outward and run from north to south. Four small triangles, read as Convergence signs, sit at the intercardinal points. Two larger triangles sit at the east and west points, pointing inward toward the diamond. Short vertical marks sit at the north and south points between the curved strokes. The fingers rest on the patch's edges and do not cover the ring, but the small scale leaves fine detail soft.

The four Convergence signs placed evenly around it focus that magic down to a single point. The larger inward-pointing triangles and the vertical marks are additional components in a symmetric arrangement and add to the targeting side of the spell. Together they form a layered spell, with an inner seal that records sound and an outer seal that drives pursuit.
effect: Records a spoken phrase and makes its target repeatedly echo it while pursuing a set destination.

Its ring looks closed, and a few tiny marks circle a central mark, but they are too small and blurred to match to any sigil or sign. Behind the disc, a larger pattern is drawn on cloth. It shows curved ring-like lines, a hollow square, and several triangles. Fingers and thumbs cover much of this pattern, and the panel edge cuts off its outer part, so it is only partly visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode reliably. No element sigil can be identified on the small disc, and its surrounding marks cannot be told apart. The larger pattern on the cloth is too covered and too cut off to read as a seal.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A manga panel showing a tied cloth pouch resting on a pile of round discs, each marked with a small star-like mark and a ring of tiny dots. Behind the pouch at the upper left, part of a larger seal ring is visible with at least two triangle shapes near its edge, which look like Convergence signs. Most of the seal, including the center where a sigil would sit, is hidden behind the pouch, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed. The marks on the discs are too small to read.
justification: The visible triangles match the Convergence sign, which focuses a spell's magic down to a single point. The sigil and the remaining signs are covered, so the element and the full set of modifiers cannot be read, and the signs cannot be combined into a full spell.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, because the sigil is hidden. The visible Convergence signs only show that the spell's magic is focused toward a single point.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed. At the center is a diamond outline flanked by two long curved vertical lines that bow in toward it. Two half-lens shapes sit at the east and west points, their tips touching those curves. Together this composite figure forms the Sigil of Calling. Short straight vertical lines sit directly north and south of the diamond. Four outlined Convergence triangles sit at the four intercardinal points, each with a point aimed toward the center. Two solid filled triangles are attached to the inside of the ring at the north and south points, both pointing inward.
justification: The central Calling figure sets the kind of magic: recording a phrase and echoing it back. The four Convergence signs are evenly spaced around it with points turned inward, which focuses the spell's magic down toward a single point. The filled triangles on the ring and the two vertical lines are not matched signs, so their exact roles cannot be read individually. Their mirrored placement at north and south suggests they belong to the outer layer of the seal, which drives pursuit of a destination, while the Calling sigil forms the inner layer that handles the recorded sound.
effect: Makes the target repeatedly echo a recorded phrase while it pursues a target destination.

name: Pouch of Calling Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a diamond, flanked east and west by two half-lens shapes whose curved sides point inward toward it. Together these form the Calling sigil. Two long vertical lines run north to south on either side of the diamond. They bow inward at the middle, where the tips of the half-lens shapes meet them. At the four intercardinal points sit four Convergence triangles, each with one point aimed toward the center. There are no filled triangles and no other signs.
justification: The Calling sigil sets the magic: it records a phrase and echoes it repeatedly. The four Convergence signs are evenly placed, each with a point aimed inward, so the magic centers down on a single point. This gives the spell a focused target to move toward. The two vertical lines have no established sign meaning on their own. The seal works as two layers: a recorded-sound part around the Calling sigil and a pursuit part around it.
effect: Records a spoken phrase and makes its target echo that phrase over and over while it travels toward a set destination.

name: Purify
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a water sigil: an S-curve flanked by two droplets, with the left droplet pointing up and the right droplet pointing down. A Refuse sign sits at the east point and another at the west point. In each, the diamond lies toward the ring and the crossed legs reach toward the sigil. Ten Purification signs, curled hooks, surround the center. Five arc over the top half from west to east, and five arc under the bottom half, mirroring the upper set.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. The many Purification signs, an asymmetric sign tied to cleaning water, direct that water magic toward separating out impurities. The two Refuse signs are directional signs that collect unwanted material and waste toward where they point. Placed on either side of the sigil, they gather the separated waste. Together these form a water-cleaning seal.
effect: Purifies wastewater by separating waste from the water, leaving it clean and collecting the unwanted material aside.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: An animated frame in which a cupped hand holds a small stack of paper with a seal drawn on the top sheet. The ring is fully visible and closed, foreshortened into an oval by the angle. A small sigil sits at the center, and its lines are consistent with a fire sigil, though the detail is soft at this size. Four signs are spaced evenly at the north, south, east and west points. Each is an arrow-like shape with a crossbar that matches the Levitation sign, with its pointed end facing inward. No other signs are visible, and nothing covers the seal.
justification: The central fire sigil sets the element to flame, and its small size relative to the ring points to a modest flame. Levitation signs float the spell's magic and any light object above the seal, with their length setting carrying weight, distance or speed. Four of them placed evenly around the center keep the effect balanced, which lets the flame gather and hover rather than drift in one direction.
effect: Creates a ball of flame that levitates directly above the seal. It can also float a light object along with the flame. The number of Levitation signs can vary without changing the basic effect.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A manga panel with a small seal drawn on a sheet of paper lying on a table, seen at a steep angle. The ring is closed. A small mark at the center resembles a fire sigil. Four short arrow-like signs sit around it, roughly at the north, south, east and west points. A wisp of drawn smoke trails down into the upper part of the seal and overlaps it. At this size and angle, the exact shapes of the sigil and signs cannot be confirmed.
justification: The central mark most likely sets the element as fire. The four evenly spaced arrow-like signs match the shape of Levitation signs, which float the magic and light objects above the seal. Evenly balanced Levitation holds the flame in place as a sphere rather than sending it in one direction. Because the glyph is tiny and partly overlapped, this reading depends on the signs being Levitation rather than Columns.
effect: If the signs are Levitation, the spell creates a ball of flame that floats directly above the seal and can lift light objects with it. If they are Columns instead, the flame also sets the surface the seal is drawn on alight.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: An anime frame of two hands over a round notebook page, one holding a pen with its nib resting on the ring line at the upper left. The seal is fully visible, and the ring appears closed. A small fire sigil sits at the center, slightly tilted. Four Levitation signs sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest and southeast points, evenly spaced, each with its arrow pointing inward toward the sigil. The fingers rest on the page's edge outside the ring and do not cover any sign.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell produces flame. Its small size relative to the ring means a modest intensity. Levitation is a directional sign that floats its target above the seal, and four of them placed evenly and pointing inward keep it balanced, which shapes the flame into a sphere and holds it in place rather than pushing it to one side.
effect: Creates a small ball of flame that floats directly above the seal. It can also lift light objects along with it. The length and number of the Levitation signs set how much weight the spell can carry.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: An anime frame of a seal drawn on a sheet of paper on the grass, viewed from above at a distance. Glowing light washes over the sheet. The ring appears closed and fully visible. Four short signs sit evenly at the north, south, east, and west points, all of similar length. Their shape fits Levitation or Columns, but at this size it is unclear whether they end in arrowheads. A small mark sits at the center where a sigil would be, too tiny and washed out by the glow to identify.
justification: Four equal signs spaced evenly around the center make a balanced seal, so the spell should act straight up from the seal rather than leaning to one side. If the signs are Levitation, the spell floats its magic above the seal. If they are Columns, it projects the magic upward as a column. The center sigil cannot be read, so the element cannot be confirmed from the glyph itself.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the image because the sigil is unreadable. Assuming the center is a fire sigil and the four signs are Levitation, the spell creates a ball of flame that floats directly above the seal and can also lift objects that are not too heavy. If the signs are Columns instead, the flame would also set the surface the seal is drawn on alight.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A line drawing of a small round disc with a seal drawn on it, lying among a ring of scattered leaves. The inner ring of the seal looks closed, and the seal is fully visible, though small. A fire sigil sits at the center, drawn rotated so its triangle points to the right, with its side strokes and stem crossing it. About four small T-shaped signs are spaced evenly around the sigil near the ring. They resemble Columns signs, but they are tiny and only roughly legible.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element to flame. It takes up a moderate share of the ring, which suggests ordinary intensity. The modifiers are spaced evenly around it, so their pull is balanced and no single direction dominates. Columns signs send the spell's effect upward as a column above the seal. A balanced fire seal of this layout is the Pyreball Seal, drawn here in its Columns form rather than with Levitation signs.
effect: Creates a ball of flame that floats directly above the seal and can carry light objects with it. In this Columns form, the surface the seal is drawn on is also set alight along with the flame.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the lower left. A large fire sigil sits at the center, taking up a good share of the ring's interior. Four Levitation signs sit evenly at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast points. Each has its crossbar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward at the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell produces flame, and its large size relative to the ring means a fairly strong flame. Levitation is a directional sign that floats its target. With four identical signs spaced evenly and all pointing inward, the lift is balanced, which shapes the flame into a sphere and holds it directly above the seal rather than sending it in any one direction. Because the ring is open, the seal will not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Once the ring is closed, it creates a ball of fire that floats directly above the seal. The Levitation signs can also lift objects that are not too heavy, and the number and length of those signs set how much weight can be carried.

name: Qifrey's Water Dragon
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. Four water sigils sit in the outer band at the north, east, south, and west points. Each is flanked by a pair of Columns signs, giving eight in total, with their crossbars toward the ring and stems pointing inward. Four Expansion signs, each made of three nested corner brackets, sit at the four intercardinal points with their corners pointing outward. Inside these is a pentagon with a short tick at each vertex pointing outward and five small water droplets just outside its edges. Within the pentagon, four Convergence triangles sit at the north, east, south, and west, each with a point facing inward. The center holds a Dragon decorative sigil: an angular, zig-zag body with fin-like strokes, a triangular head at the upper right, and a curved tail below.
justification: The four water sigils make this a water spell. The Dragon sigil at the center shapes that water into a dragon. The pentagon with droplets is a variant of the Flower sigil, with its arches replaced by water droplets, and it gives the water the form of a water lily. The inward-pointing Convergence signs draw the surrounding water together to a single point so the spell can use it. The Expansion signs have their corners pointing outward, which makes the shape grow. The eight Columns signs are evenly balanced around the ring, so they drive the magic straight out from the seal.
effect: Draws water from nearby clouds, and likely from bodies of water, and forms it into a giant dragon made of water. The dragon then turns into a water lily before the spell stops working.

name: Qifrey's Water Dragon
description: A manga page with several panels. Most panels show figures and a large dragon shape, with no glyph in them. At the bottom right of the lowest panel, a small slice of a seal shows along the panel border, with part of the ring's edge curving across it. A few signs are partly visible on this slice. One resembles a Selection sign, a square crossed by lines. Another resembles an Orb sign, a circle with a vertical line. Fragments of other marks sit beside them but are too small or too cut off to name. The center of the seal, any sigil, and the rest of the ring lie outside the panel, so it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: Only a narrow edge of the seal is visible and no sigil can be seen, so the element of the spell is unknown. The few signs that can be made out are modifiers. A Selection-like sign would limit the effect to the object it is drawn on, and an Orb-like sign would gather material in a spherical space. Without the sigil and the remaining signs, these fragments cannot be combined into a spell.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, because the visible fragment shows no sigil and too few signs to identify the spell.

name: Rainbringer Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal in black ink on a white background, with the ring closed. A large Rain sign fills most of the interior, drawn slightly tilted: a square with inward-curving sides, with a set of about three parallel lines crossing each side and reaching out toward the ring. A water sigil sits in the open center of the Rain sign, turned on its side, with its S-curve between the two droplets. No other signs are present.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works on water. The Rain sign is semi-directional and, when not inverted, summons its target; a sigil can be placed in its center, as it is here. Together they call water down from above. The sigil is moderate in size relative to the ring, so the intensity is moderate. Because the line work and ring are loose and uneven, the result may vary, since the quality of the ring strongly shapes this spell.
effect: Summons rain. Water falls from above, either as a single mass that drops abruptly or as gentle, gradual rainfall. The quality of the ring and the sign lines plays a significant role in which of these happens.

name: Rainbringer Seal
description: An anime frame of a stack of round paper discs held from the side by a hand, with a pen nib resting on the top disc. The seal on the top disc is fully visible, seen at an angle. A water sigil, two drops flanking an S-curve, sits at the center inside a Rain sign: a four-pointed star with curved, inward-bowing edges, its points facing north, east, south and west, with three parallel lines crossing each of the four diagonal corners. The Rain sign is drawn in its normal orientation, not inverted. A thin ring runs near the edge of the disc. The pen nib touches it on the west side, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is closed. The water sigil is fairly large within the ring.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The Rain sign surrounds the sigil, which sits in its empty center, and in its normal orientation it summons the spell's material from above rather than pushing it away. A water sigil inside an upright Rain sign therefore brings down water as rainfall. The fairly large sigil suggests a moderately strong effect. How evenly the ring is drawn changes how the rain manifests.
effect: Summons rain, making water fall from above onto the area. Depending on the quality of the ring, the water either gathers into an orb overhead that drops all at once or falls gently and gradually like natural rainfall.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a wind sigil drawn as a horizontal double spiral, with no flanking strokes visible. Two smaller fire sigils sit at the north and south points, each with its apex pointing toward the center, so the northern one appears upside down. A Crosshair sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, for two in total.
justification: The large central wind sigil sets the main element, so the spell moves air. The two smaller fire sigils add heat at a lower intensity, which makes this a mixed wind and fire spell. Crosshair directs a seal's magic at whatever its shorter ends point toward, so the two Crosshair signs aim the heat into the surrounding air. Together they produce moving, heated air.
effect: Creates warm winds that evaporate moisture and dry objects within the seal's radius.

name: Rainflinger
description: A line drawing of two hands holding an unrolled scroll with an oval seal drawn on it. The ring appears closed, though the right thumb rests over its lower-right edge. A wind sigil sits at the center, drawn as an S-curve with short dashes on either side. Two smaller fire sigils flank it, one to the upper left and one to the lower right, both tilted. Small Crosshair signs mark the north and south of the ring, with a few loose dashes near them. The signs are drawn loosely and at small size, but each one can be identified.
justification: The central wind sigil sets the main element as moving air. The two smaller fire sigils add heat at a lower intensity than the wind, because they are smaller relative to the ring. Crosshair is a directional sign that aims the seal's magic at whatever its shorter ends point toward. Here the Crosshair signs direct the heat onto the moving air, so the seal produces warm wind.
effect: Sends warm wind across the area of the seal, evaporating moisture and drying anything within its radius.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as a double ring: an outer circle and an inner circle, both closed, so the ring is closed. The inner circle is empty, with no sigil at the center. Four small Repetition signs sit on the band between the two circles at the north, east, south and west points. Between them, eight groups each consist of a Convergence triangle flanked by two Columns signs, giving sixteen Columns and eight Convergence in all. Each Columns sign has its crossbar toward the outer circle and its stem toward the center. Each Convergence triangle has one point aimed inward.
justification: No element sigil is present. The four Repetition signs take that role, and Repetition is the sign that continuously resets a target to the state it had when the spell first touched it. The Columns signs create column-shaped areas of effect and set the range or quantity of the magic. Their even spacing around the ring balances the effect so it pushes in no single direction. The inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and pack loose particles tightly together. Because the Repetition signs sit on the band rather than in the middle, the empty inner circle is left as the space where the target rests.
effect: Continuously reverts the target to the state it had when the spell first affected it, so any change is undone and the object stays like new. This restores its physical form and its temperature, so it can make soft objects spring back into shape, keep things from rotting, or repair damage.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of two concentric rings, both closed. The inner circle is empty, with no sigil at the center. Four Repetition glyphs sit in the band between the rings, at the north, east, south and west points, each rotated to follow the curve of the ring. Each of the four arcs between them holds the same sequence: a Columns sign, a Convergence triangle, and a second Columns sign. That makes eight Columns signs in total, each with its crossbar toward the outer ring and its stem toward the center. Each Convergence triangle sits with one point angled inward.
justification: No element sigil is present. Repetition takes that role instead, repeated four times around the band, and it remains a sign that sets the time-resetting behavior. The Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect, and because their stems all point inward they aim it at the empty inner circle. The Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and pack it tightly. Together they concentrate the resetting effect on whatever occupies the inner circle. The arrangement is symmetric in all four directions, so no direction is favored.
effect: Continuously resets the target to the state it was in when the spell first affected it, physical form and temperature included, so it stays like new. This keeps soft material springy, stops things from rotting, and undoes damage or other changes.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a gap at the lower left. An outer band of sixteen Convergence triangles runs around the inside of the ring, each with one point aimed inward. Inside that band are six Repetition signs in a hexagonal arrangement: one north, one south, and one at each of the four diagonals. At the center sits a circle with four Diamond-shaped points straddling its edge at north, south, east and west, plus four short ticks on the circle at the intercardinal points. No element sigil is present.
justification: There is no element sigil; Repetition takes that role here, as one of the few signs that can stand in for a sigil, and six copies multiply its time-resetting effect around the seal. The sixteen inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and draw it tightly together at the center. The central circle with four Diamonds suggests the effect is limited to the contents held by the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn.
effect: Once the ring is closed, the seal continuously resets its target to the state it was in when the spell first took hold, keeping it like new by restoring its form and temperature whenever it changes, for example by stopping food from rotting. The Diamonds likely confine this effect to whatever the marked container holds.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. The center holds a Repetition sign in place of a sigil, drawn as a small inner circle inside a larger circle, with a long S-shaped stroke running through both and sweeping out into open arcs at the upper left and lower right. Six Columns signs sit in two groups of three, one group arcing from the west-northwest to the north and the other mirrored from the south to the southeast. Each Columns sign lies sideways along the ring, with its stem pointing counterclockwise. At the northeast and southwest sit two large X-shaped crosses whose strokes meet off-center. They resemble Collection signs without the closing bar. No element sigil is present.
justification: With no element sigil, the central Repetition sign drives the spell. It resets whatever it affects to the state the object had when the spell first touched it. The Columns signs, all turned the same way around the ring, push that effect in a rotating, column-shaped area rather than one straight direction. The two X-shaped crosses, if read as Collection, gather material from around the seal for the spell to act on. The ring is open, so the spell is not active as drawn.
effect: Continuously reverts a target object to its earlier state after any change, keeping it like new. It can restore an object's shape and temperature, keep things from rotting, or make soft materials spring back to their original form.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible diagram of a large seal with a thick outer ring, ring closed, and a smaller closed inner ring at its center. Four Repetition signs, each in its own small circle, sit on the outer band at the north, east, south, and west points. Between them sit groups of a Convergence triangle flanked by two Columns signs. Inside the inner ring, a Billow sign sits at the center with Collection signs to the north and south and Convergence triangles to the east and west. Four small circles around it each hold a small seal with an earth sigil, Columns signs, and Crushing signs. Three labeled insets sit outside the main seal: a small earth seal labeled Wall Breaker, a Billow-centered cluster labeled Billow Cluster, and a lone Repetition sign labeled Sign of Repetition.
justification: This is a compound seal with no single element sigil at its center. The four small earth seals with Columns and Crushing are Wall Breaker seals, which crush stone into sand. The central Billow cluster works as follows: Collection gathers that material, Convergence packs the loose particles together, and Billow, sitting in place of a sigil, turns them into a soft cloud-like mass. The outer band of Repetition signs, flanked by Convergence and Columns, keeps resetting the result to its original state. Together these let the crushed sand take its shape and keep returning to it.
effect: Crushes stone into sand, gathers and packs it into a soft, billowing bed that is comfortable to rest on, and continuously reverts it to its original state whenever it is disturbed or changed.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A manga panel. A hand grips a round, flat object seen almost edge-on, so the seal on its face is heavily foreshortened. The ring follows the rim and is visible along the right edge, but the left side curves away behind the hand and the thickness of the rim, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. Two Repetition glyphs are clearly visible down the middle: circles with an inner spiral, a central dot, and short tick lines. Partial copies of the same glyph appear at the top and bottom edges. Between them sits a lumpy, cloud-like cluster of scalloped shapes around an oval with dots and lines, possibly a Billow sign, but it is too distorted to identify with confidence. Along the right inner edge runs a row of small triangles resembling Convergence signs, alternating with chevron and zigzag marks that may be Crushing or Collection signs. The left portion of the seal is hidden.
justification: Repetition can stand in the center in place of a sigil, and here several Repetition glyphs repeated across the seal make Repetition the core of the spell, so the seal's job is to keep resetting its target. The ring of Convergence-like triangles around the edge would focus the magic and pack loose material tightly, and the possible Crushing, Collection, and Billow-like marks would gather and shape material. These modifiers cannot be confirmed at this angle and only refine how the resetting is applied.
effect: Continuously reverts the target object to the state it was in when the spell first affected it, so it stays like new and snaps back if changed. This reading rests on the clearly visible Repetition glyphs and assumes the hidden left side carries the same arrangement as the visible right side.

name: Repetition Seal
description: Two manga panels. In the left panel a round wooden lid with a seal drawn on it is held up near the left edge, and the panel border cuts off its left side. A Repetition glyph sits at the center: a ring with an inner curl around a central dot. Diagonal strokes cross through it in an X-like pattern. Small marks run around the inner edge of the ring but are too small to identify. Because the left side is cut off, it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. The right panel shows barrels and a loose lid with no legible seal.
justification: Repetition can sit in the center in place of a sigil. Here it takes that central spot, so the seal works on time rather than on an element. The surrounding modifiers are illegible at this size, so only the core behavior can be read.
effect: Continuously resets the target to the state it was in when the spell first affected it, keeping it like new. The exact variant cannot be read from the image because the surrounding signs are illegible.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A manga panel showing a round object with a seal drawn on it. A Repetition sign sits at the center, drawn as a small circle with an inner curve around a dot. Small signs ring it: X-shaped marks that resemble Collection signs on the right and lower left, Y-shaped marks near the top and lower left, and a row of three T-shaped marks along the bottom that resemble Columns signs. The upper-left quarter is covered by heavy dark hatching and a pointed object, which hide the signs and the ring there. The ring looks unbroken where it can be seen, but its hidden portion cannot be checked, so it is not known whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: The Repetition sign takes the place of a sigil at the center, so this is a repetition seal. Repetition continuously resets what the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first took hold. The surrounding signs are too small and partly hidden to identify with certainty. They would set what material the spell targets and how it is shaped.
effect: Continuously reverts the target object to its earlier state whenever it changes, keeping it like new. The exact variant cannot be determined because the surrounding signs are obscured.

name: Ring of Fire
description: A manga panel of two hands holding a stack of round discs, with a pen nib touching the top disc. A small, foreshortened mark that resembles a fire sigil, a triangle with short strokes, sits near the middle of the top disc, next to a smaller cross-like stroke. The pen and the steep angle hide most of the drawing. No ring edge and no surrounding signs can be made out.
justification: The triangular mark points to a fire sigil, which sets the spell as fire magic. The signs that would set how the fire behaves cannot be read, and the ring cannot be seen, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed.
effect: The visible sigil indicates a spell that creates fire. How the fire is shaped or directed cannot be determined from the image.

name: Ring of Fire
description: A manga panel of a caped, hatted figure in the middle of a large circle of flames, with heavy action lines and sound effect lettering on both sides. The round shape is made of fire, not ink, and no ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The circle of flames is a magical effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Rising Platform of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the lower left. A large water sigil fills the center. Four Levitation signs sit near the north, east, south and west points, each turned sideways so its arrow runs along the ring rather than toward or away from the center. Together they form a pinwheel pointing clockwise. Four Columns signs sit at the four intercardinal points, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing at the sigil.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring makes the effect strong. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect. Four of them placed evenly means the column is balanced and rises straight rather than leaning to one side. Levitation floats the target. Because these directional signs are turned sideways and spaced evenly around the ring, their sideways pulls cancel out, leaving only the lift. Together these signs make a lifting column of water.
effect: Generates a surging column of water that lifts the object the seal is drawn on straight up into the air. The ring is open, so the spell is not yet active.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel of a figure crouched atop a rising surge of water, with part of a hat brim at the right edge. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The wave is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel showing a pair of boots stepping on the ground beneath the hem of a robe. Several curved ink strokes on the ground form arcs that look like parts of a seal's ring, possibly two concentric arcs, with sections passing under and behind the boots. No sigil and no signs are visible. The interior of the arcs is blank or covered by the boots, and the edges of the curves run out of frame or fade into the ground texture, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: Only ring-like arcs are legible. Without a visible sigil or any signs, there is nothing to decode, and the element and modifiers cannot be read from this image.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, since no sigil or signs are visible.

name: Rising Wave
description: A manga panel with a figure standing on a large seal drawn on the ground, seen at a steep angle. Only the far arc of the ring shows along the bottom edge of the panel, so it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed. Along the inside of that arc, small signs alternate between T-shaped Columns signs and V-shaped Regions signs. The figure's boots cover part of the arc. The center of the seal, where a sigil would sit, is out of frame, and so are any inner signs.
justification: Columns sets a column-shaped area of effect, pushed in a given direction. Regions sets where magic manifests relative to the ring. description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two rings. The outer band is a double ring packed with repeated chevron markings, matching the Windows sign, which lines the seal like an extra ring. Inside it, a thicker inner ring holds the main body. It appears to have a small break at the upper left, so it reads as ring open there. At the center is a Concealment sign: an eight-armed star with four eye shapes set on its diagonals. Four Expansion signs, each a set of three nested right-angle brackets, frame it at the intercardinal points with their corners pointing outward. Stability and Level Planes signs, each made of three wavy lines, sit in the four gaps between the Expansion signs at north, south, east and west. Stability and Level Planes balance the target in a plane in the air, which supplies the floating. The eight Columns signs are balanced around the ring, so they give a column-shaped area of effect with no lean in any one direction. The arrangement reads as an expansion effect and a levitation effect drawn together in one ring.

The outer band, between the outer and middle rings, holds four Repetition signs at the north, east, south, and west points, each sitting across the inner edge of the band. Each quadrant between them has a Columns sign, then a Convergence triangle, then another Columns sign, for eight Columns and four Convergence in total. Each Columns sign has its crossbar on the outer side and its stem pointing toward the center, and each Convergence triangle has one point facing the center. Each of the four linked rings pairs an earth sigil with Crushing and Columns signs, which is the core that crushes ground into fine sand. Their links feed that sand into the central cloud. The outer band uses Repetition in place of sigils, together with Convergence and Columns. Convergence packs loose particles tightly, and Repetition keeps resetting the cloud to its first state, so it cannot lose its consistency.
effect: Crushes the surrounding ground into fine, soft sand and gathers it into a large, fluffy cloud. The cloud is strong enough to hold up even a dragon. Because it keeps resetting to its original state, it regains its shape once the weight is removed.

description: A fully visible seal on a clean background made of two concentric rings. The outer ring is open at the lower left, and the inner ring is broken only where two signs cross it. A Water sigil sits at the center of the inner ring. In the band between the rings, a sideways Wind sigil sits at the east point and another at the west point. Six Columns signs sit in the band with their bars toward the outer ring and their stems pointing inward: one at north, one at south, and one at each of the four diagonal positions near the east and west sides. Four Cooling signs, each a slanted line with dots on either side, sit between the north and south Columns and their neighbors. Two Gathering signs, one at north and one at south, cross the inner ring with their arrowheads pointing in toward the Water sigil.
justification: The Water sigil sets the core element, so the inner ring is a water spell. The outer ring adds effects to it. Its two Wind sigils move the surrounding air, and the Cooling signs chill it. The inward-pointing Gathering signs actively draw material in toward the water core. The six evenly spaced Columns are balanced, so they direct the gathered magic toward the center rather than any one side. Together, cooled, moving air gives up its moisture, which is pulled into the central water spell.
effect: Gathers moisture from the surrounding air and stores it as an orb of fresh water.

name: Wall Bend
description: A manga panel of a figure in a pointed hat and cape reaching up toward a brick wall, pressing a small square card against the bricks. The card carries drawn markings, but they are tiny and partly covered by the hand and fingers. No ring, sigil, or sign can be made out.
justification: Nothing to decode. Some markings are present on the card, but no element sigil or individual sign is legible.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Wall Breaker Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a gap in its lower left between roughly the seven and eight o'clock positions. An earth sigil sits at the center: a top bar, a vertical stem, an angled V-shaped body, and the two side dots. It has an extra horizontal bar drawn across its base. One Columns sign sits at the east point and one at the west point. Each has its crossbar at the outer end near the ring and its stem pointing toward the sigil. A large Crushing sign sits at the north point and another at the south point. They mirror each other, with their open ends facing the center.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on solid matter such as stone, wood, and soil. The two Crushing signs, set at right angles to the Columns, break the targeted material into pieces. Because these Crushing signs are large, the pieces are ground very small. They are drawn in their normal orientation, not inverted, so the effect is pulverizing rather than reforming. The paired Columns direct and push that force along their axis. This is the arrangement of the Wall Breaker seal. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate until it is closed.
effect: When the ring is closed, the spell breaks through the solid object it is drawn on and grinds the material down to dust or sand.

name: Wall of Wind
description: A manga panel with a seal drawn in ink. The upper part is covered by a large white shape, and a dark vertical line crosses the right side, so the full ring cannot be seen and it is unclear whether it is open or closed. A wind sigil sits near the center. Along the left side runs a cluster of small triangles matching Convergence signs. Along the bottom edge is a row of about five inverted Columns signs. Between the sigil and that row is a curved, semicircular line with small marks along its edge. The rest of the seal is hidden or cut off.
justification: The wind sigil sets the spell to move air. Inverted Columns manifest horizontally instead of vertically and spread their effect outward, so the air is pushed out from the seal rather than up. Convergence focuses the magic about a single point, which keeps the moving air centered on the seal. The semicircular sign on the Columns side frames that outward push around the sigil. Together these produce a ring of moving air around a center. The hidden portions may hold more signs that cannot be read here.
effect: Creates a circular wall of air that is difficult for objects or people to pass through, which can be used to contain people or animals. This assumes the hidden part of the seal does not change the core arrangement that is visible.

name: Wand of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with the ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, enclosed by a Holding sign whose two curved arms bracket it on the left and right, each ending in a small dot near the bottom. At the north point is a cluster of three signs: a central sign pointing upward that reads as Dispersion, flanked by two Columns signs that mirror each other on either side. At the south point, below the sigil, is a Pointing sign.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water magic. Holding keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Pointing makes the water taper into a cone. The two mirrored Columns signs define the broad base of that shape, and Dispersion pushes the effect outward, so it takes form outside the confines of the ring rather than inside it.
effect: Shapes water into a large pen nib that hovers below the seal at an angle. Conjuring ink can be poured into the water to saturate it, turning the nib into a tool for drawing large seals across stone, sand, or other broad flat surfaces.

name: Wand of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a gap at the lower left. A water sigil sits at the center, large relative to the ring, enclosed by a tall Holding sign whose two curved strokes wrap around it, with a dot outside each lower end. North of the sigil is a Dispersion sign drawn as a T with its arc above the crossbar, pointing outward toward the top of the ring. It is flanked by two Columns signs turned on their sides and mirrored, one on each side, with their stems facing the Dispersion sign. South of the sigil is a single Pointing sign, a triangle crossing a horizontal bar with a hook curling up at each end.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its large size points to a strong effect. Holding keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. The mirrored Columns signs set a column-shaped body that forms the base of the shape, and Pointing tapers the water into a cone, so together they make a nib. Dispersion lets the magic spill outward past the seal, so the form appears outside the ring instead of within it. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn until it is closed.
effect: Forms water into a large hovering pen nib that sits at an angle below the seal. Conjuring ink poured into it saturates the water, so it can draw large seals across stone, sand, or other wide flat surfaces.

name: Wand of Water
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, enclosed by a Holding sign: two tall curved brackets on the east and west sides, each with a dot beside its lower end. A Pointing sign sits south of the sigil. At the north point is a T-shaped sign with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the sigil, shaped like Columns but without the curved stroke of Dispersion. It is flanked by two Columns signs turned sideways and mirrored, with their crossbars on the outer sides and their stems pointing inward toward the north sign.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works with water. The Holding sign around the sigil keeps the water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. The two Columns signs define the broad base of the form, and the Pointing sign tapers the water into a cone. The north sign sits where Dispersion belongs and acts like Dispersion, letting the effect manifest outside the ring instead of within it.
effect: Shapes water into a large pen nib that hovers below the seal at an angle. Conjuring ink can be poured into the water to saturate it, turning the nib into a giant pen. It can then draw large seals on stone, sand, or any flat, expansive surface.

name: Water Bolt
description: A manga panel showing a large oval seal drawn on a flat surface, seen at an angle. The left and top edges of the ring are visible. The right side is cut off by an overlapping blank shape, and the bottom is cut off by the panel border, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed. A row of Piercing signs, each a long line through a diamond, runs diagonally across the middle of the seal. Four of them are legible, and a further line near the left is partly hidden. About four V-shaped Regions signs sit spread around the row, all pointing the same way, toward the lower edge of the panel. Splashing water and a sleeved hand cover the upper left, and a curved shape near the center left may be the central sigil, but the splash hides it too much to identify.
justification: The Piercing signs make the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many are created. Regions signs that all point to the same side send the magic in that direction. Taken together, the row of Piercing signs between the matching Regions signs fires a volley of bolts in one direction. The element cannot be confirmed from the hidden center. Assuming it is a water sigil and that the hidden part holds a fifth Piercing sign, the layout matches a seal of five bolts.
effect: Creates five bolts of water that surge forward at an upward angle. This assumes the obscured center is a water sigil and that the cut-off part of the seal completes the row of five Piercing signs.

name: Water Bolt
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A small water sigil sits near the bottom, drawn lying on its side. Five Piercing signs stand upright in a row across the middle in a shallow arch, with the center one highest and the outer ones lowest. Four Regions signs sit between and beside them: two high, above the gaps flanking the central Piercing sign, and two lower, just inside the ring at the west and east edges. All four point the same way, toward the bottom of the seal.
justification: The water sigil sets the element. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many form, so five signs give five bolts. Regions signs that all point to the same side send the magic in that direction, which gives the volley a single shared heading. As drawn, the ring is open, so the seal will not activate until the gap at the bottom is closed.
effect: Creates five bolts of water that surge forward together at an upward angle as an offensive volley. The more Piercing signs are drawn, the more bolts are produced.

name: Water Bolt
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed. A water sigil sits just above the center of the inner ring. Across the top are three Sights Set signs, each with its arrow pointing at the sigil. The north one has a diamond resting on the outer ring and an arrow running straight down. The northwest and northeast ones have square heads on the outer ring and arrows running diagonally inward. Two Convergence triangles sit between these three arrows. At the east and west points sit two Strengthening signs, turned sideways so their triangles point in toward the sigil. Below the sigil, a single Piercing sign runs down toward the south edge of the inner ring. It is flanked by two Regions signs whose points angle inward toward the center.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. A water sigil with Piercing and Regions signs is the core of a water bolt. Piercing makes the magic manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many form, so one sign means one bolt. The three Sights Set signs aimed at the sigil let the caster aim the spell at a chosen target. Convergence focuses the water to a single point and packs it tightly. The Strengthening signs make it harder and more durable. The inward-pointing Regions signs control where the magic manifests relative to the seal.
effect: Forms a single focused, hardened bolt of water and fires it at a target the caster aims at. It is an offensive water projectile.

name: Water Bolt
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with two concentric rings, both closed. A water sigil sits in the upper center. Above it, three Sights Set signs point inward at the sigil: one from the north and one each from the northwest and northeast, with their diamond tails resting on the outer ring. Two Convergence signs sit between them, one on each side of the north Sights Set. Strengthening signs, drawn tilted, mark the west and east. Below the sigil, three Piercing signs stand side by side. Two Regions signs at the southwest and southeast point inward toward the center.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Piercing makes the water manifest as projectiles, and the number of Piercing signs sets how many, so three signs give three bolts. Sights Set aims the spell at a chosen target. Convergence focuses the magic toward a single point. Strengthening makes the result harder and more durable. The inward-pointing Regions signs keep the magic forming within the seal before it is sent out.
effect: Creates three hardened bolts of water and fires them as offensive projectiles at a target the caster aims at.

name: Water Cage
description: A manga panel showing two seals joined by a connecting line. The larger seal on the left is an oval with its ring closed and a water sigil at the center. It is ringed by small, roughly drawn signs. Chevron-shaped marks resembling Regions signs and zigzag marks resembling Crushing signs can be made out, but the remaining marks are too small and sketchy to identify. The smaller seal on the right, ring closed, holds a single Pulling sign whose arrow points along the connecting line toward the larger seal. Its right edge sits near the panel border.
justification: The water sigil sets the larger seal's element. The Regions signs set where the magic manifests relative to the ring. Pointed toward the Crushing signs, they appear to shape the water into a bounded form rather than letting it spread freely, though the unreadable signs leave the full arrangement uncertain. The smaller linked seal has no sigil of its own and only a Pulling sign, which pulls things toward where its arrow points. Here the arrow points at the larger seal.
effect: Creates a spherical cage of water around the target. The linked Pulling seal draws the target toward the larger seal so it is caught inside the cage more easily.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel of an oval seal held between two hands, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center. On either side of it is a tall stacked sign matching Mimicry, one west and one east, with fingertips overlapping their outer edges. Along the north edge is a row of small marks: what look like two Columns signs pointing in opposite directions, with a small figure between them that is too small to identify. Along the south edge is an alternating row of five marks: three short vertical strokes and two Regions signs pointing downward. Parts of the left and right edges of the ring are hidden by the fingers.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and shapes water. The Mimicry signs beside it guide the movements of whatever form the spell takes. The opposed Columns signs and the downward Regions signs control where the water manifests relative to the seal, and the vertical strokes between the Regions signs cannot be identified. The figure along the north edge is not legible enough to confirm what shape the water takes, though its place between the Columns fits a shape-giving sigil.
effect: Creates a horse out of water that can be mounted, guided, and controlled like a regular horse, with Mimicry guiding its movements. This assumes the illegible figure at the north edge is the sigil that gives the water a horse's shape, and that the covered edges hold nothing beyond what is visible.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel of a large surge of splashing water rising upward, with a figure riding on it and another figure running below amid speed lines. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The water is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel of a horse-shaped figure pulling a cart along a rocky, wet path, with a figure in a pointed hat seated on the cart. A cylindrical fitting is mounted at the horse's head. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The horse and cart are effects and scenery, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga illustration of dozens of round discs, each carrying a seal, falling around a figure in a pointed hat. The matching seal is on a disc at the lower left, ring closed, drawn very small. A water sigil sits at the center. Above it is a figure that reads as a horse decorative sigil, and on either side of the water sigil are vertical signs that match Mimicry. Along the bottom of the ring runs a row of small marks, some of which look like Regions signs pointing downward. The neighbouring disc touches its lower right edge. At this scale the individual strokes, including any Columns signs beside the horse sigil, cannot be read with certainty.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water. The horse decorative sigil sculpts that water into a horse shape. Mimicry signs make the shaped water imitate the movements of what the decorative sigil depicts. The downward-pointing Regions signs set where the magic manifests relative to the seal. The remaining marks are too small to decode, so this reading rests on the clearly visible sigils and the general layout.
effect: Creates a horse out of water that moves like a real horse and can be mounted, guided and controlled by the caster. This assumes the unreadable small signs match the rest of the layout.

name: Water Orb
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower right. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn as an S-curve flanked by two teardrops, one pointing up and one pointing down. A Columns sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, each with its crossbar near the ring and its stem reaching toward the center. Four Orb signs, each a circle crossed by a diagonal line, sit at the four intercardinal points. Their diagonals are mirrored left to right, so the arrangement is symmetric.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The four Orb signs are non-directional and define a spherical space above the seal where the controlled material collects. Material fills that space from the bottom up and stays subject to gravity. The two balanced Columns signs push the effect upward in a column, lifting that space above the seal. The sigil's orientation does not change its known effect. The ring is open, so the seal will not activate until it is closed.
effect: Creates an invisible spherical container above the seal that holds water. Water poured directly into it fills the sphere from the bottom up, the way it would fill a cup.

name: Water Rose
description: A manga panel showing a rose shape made of liquid rising on a long stem, surrounded by scattered droplets and splashes. A hand holding a pen sits at the right, and another hand at the bottom holds a dark, flat object seen edge-on. A hat brim curves along the left side. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: Nothing to decode. The rose and droplets are an effect, not a glyph, and the object in the lower hand shows no markings from this angle.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Waterflinger
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black ink on a plain background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center. Two smaller fire sigils mark the north and south points, mirroring each other across the center. One Crosshair sign sits at the east point and one at the west point, flanking the water sigil.
justification: The large central water sigil sets the main element, and the two smaller fire sigils add heat at a lower intensity, since a sigil's size relative to the ring sets its strength. Crosshair makes the seal's magic target whatever its shorter ends point at. Here the two Crosshairs sit on either side of the water sigil, so the fire's heat is likely directed at water.
effect: The exact effect is unknown. It likely targets water with heat to evaporate it, driving the water away.

name: Watersculpture
description: A manga panel of a horse-like figure made of water rising from a pool beside stone walls, with a figure watching from the lower right. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The water figure is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Watersculpture
description: A manga panel of two hands holding a cut-glass cup as a stream of liquid pours into it, with sound effects above. The surface of the liquid swirls into a rough shape. The cup and the saucer beneath it carry lattice and petal patterns, but no ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The patterns on the cup and saucer are ornament rather than a glyph, and the shape in the liquid is an effect, not a seal.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Watershot Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the lower left. A water sigil sits at the center, filling a moderate share of the ring. Eight Columns signs surround it, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point. Each has its crossbar facing outward toward the ring and its stem pointing inward. Seven of them are short and roughly equal in length. The Columns sign at the south point has a much longer stem that reaches up nearly to the sigil.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell works with water, and its moderate size gives a moderate intensity. Columns signs make magic manifest as a column or beam, and their number sets the range or quantity of magic produced. When all Columns signs are equal, the beam rises straight up from the seal. Lengthening a Columns sign adds pressure or power in its direction, so the elongated south sign makes the stream lean or push in that direction rather than rise straight up. The open ring means the seal is inactive until the ring is closed.
effect: Creates a stream of water that shoots up from the seal in a column. With all eight Columns signs of equal length, it fires straight up. Here the longer south sign adds pressure on one side, so the stream is directed off vertical.

name: Windowway Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background made of three concentric circles, all closed. The outer band, between the outermost and middle circles, is packed with a continuous run of identical zigzag, lightning bolt-shaped marks all the way around. The inner band, between the middle and innermost circles, holds a continuous run of identical chevron marks resembling Regions signs. Every chevron points clockwise along the band rather than inward or outward. The central space inside the innermost circle is empty, with no sigil or other sign.
justification: Bands of many identical simple markings lining the seal like extra rings are the Windows sign. Windows connects two spaces that are not physically connected, so the repeated zigzag band acts as Windows lining the spell. The chevron band behaves like Regions signs set to point around the ring rather than in or out. They likely direct where the passage manifests and keep it on the ring itself. The seal has no sigil because its magic is spatial rather than elemental. No location mark sits in the center, so the destination is not specified by anything visible.
effect: Opens a gateway between two distant locations, letting someone pass through from one place to the other. The seal works only as one of a matched pair, each drawn uniquely so it links to its partner and no other.

name: Beldaruit's Smoke Sculpture
description: A manga panel showing a close-up of a large, dense seal drawn on a flat surface. A left hand rests flat across the lower left of the seal and a right hand holds a pen over the right side, hiding several areas. No ring is visible, so it cannot be told whether the ring is open or closed, and the panel edges cut off the seal on every side, leaving it only partly visible. Many small Columns-like signs run in rows and diagonal lines across the upper middle. A vertical axis runs down the center with stacked shapes: at the top, a form with teardrop marks resembling a water sigil; below it, branching arrow shapes resembling Gathering or Levitation signs; then small circles and a figure-like shape. Asterisk-like marks sit at the upper left and upper right. A row of chevrons along a horizontal line at the lower right resembles Gathering or Pulling signs. Small dashed curves and paired T-shaped marks fill the lower center. Much of the seal is too small, hidden, or out of frame to name with confidence.
justification: The large number of Columns signs suggests the magic is raised and directed upward in several places. The stacked arrow signs along the central axis suggest material is drawn in and lifted. However, no central sigil can be identified with certainty. The hands and the panel edges hide large parts of the layout, so the visible signs cannot be combined into a full reading.
effect: The full seal forms a fake dragon out of smoke that can fly through the air and roar. The visible portion is consistent with lifting and shaping material, but it does not confirm this effect on its own.

name: Billowing Collection
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. A four-lobed Billow sign sits at the center where a sigil would normally go. Four Collection signs surround it, one each at the north, east, south and west points. Each has its barred end toward the ring and its open side facing inward toward the center. No element sigil is present.
justification: Billow is a sign, but here it takes the place of a sigil at the center. It sets the core behavior of the spell, which is turning material into a fluffy cloud. The four Collection signs gather material above and around the seal so the spell can use it. Their open sides face inward, which is their usual orientation. They are evenly spaced, so the effect is balanced on all sides rather than pushed in one direction. With no element sigil, the spell is not tied to fire, water, earth or wind. It works on whatever material is brought to it.
effect: Gathers any material directed into the seal and converts it into a soft, fluffy cloud that is very comfortable to sit on.

name: Bird of Light Beacon
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black line on a white background, ring closed. The center holds a light sigil: a small square set inside a diamond, crossed by long diagonal strokes that form an X through it. A Launch sign sits at the north point, opening toward the center. A Dispersion sign sits at the south point, its stem pointing toward the sigil and its curve facing outward. At the east and west points are mirrored wing-like figures, each made of two stacked curved arcs with a small inward-pointing notch where they meet. Each figure has three short dashes on its outer side, beyond the arcs.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the seal creates and shapes light. The east and west figures mirror each other and read as the two halves of a bird design. They give the light the shape of a bird. Launch at the north sends that light out in a strong but brief burst, which carries it high into the air. Dispersion at the south lets the magic pour outward instead of holding it to a fixed beam. Together these make a loose, outward-moving bird of light rather than a steady lamp.
effect: Creates a bird made of light that bursts upward and flies around for some time before fading. It can serve to entertain, to signal for help, or to distract.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A fully visible seal with a thick, closed ring, surrounded by motion lines and printed in heavy halftone dots. Two pale glare spots, one on the left interior and one on the upper right, wash out parts of the seal. At the center is a curved, hooked stroke with a dot inside it, closer to the inner curl of the Repetition sign than to any clear element sigil. Around it sit about six or seven small marks, all blurred. These include a branching, footprint-like mark with several prongs to the northwest, a hooked mark to the west, short parallel strokes to the southwest, an inverted-V mark to the south that could be Regions or Launch, and a triangular mark to the east that could be Convergence or Strengthening. None of the surrounding signs can be matched with confidence.
justification: The ring is closed, so the seal would be active. The halftone and glare blur the glyph too much to identify the center glyph or any surrounding sign with certainty. If the central curl is Repetition, it would hold the object in its original state rather than set an element. The branching and arrow-like marks around it cannot be confirmed, so the modifiers cannot be decoded.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the visible glyph. The seal is known to let the pennant it is drawn on be steered by the caster, wrapping it around people and objects to bind them. The signs that would confirm this are not legible here.

name: Floating Drops
description: A manga page with several panels. In the top middle panel, a hand holds a round dish with a seal drawn on it. A wind sigil is visible at the center. Small X-shaped and short stroke marks are scattered around it toward the edge of the ring, but they are too small to match to specific signs or count reliably, and it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. In the top left panel, a dish is held near a face, but its drawn surface is not visible. In the top right panel, a pen draws on a round object held in a hand. An S-shaped glyph resembling the wind sigil and a few curls beside it are visible there, and the rest is covered by the hand and pen. The large lower panel shows no readable glyph.
justification: The central wind sigil sets the spell as one that moves air. The small marks near the ring may be paired Regions signs, one normal and one inverted, pointing toward each other. That arrangement would restrict the magic to the ring itself. Water sigils beside the center would add water as a second element. None of these can be confirmed at this size, so only the wind sigil is read with certainty.
effect: Likely creates drops of water that float in the air and form only along the seal's ring. This assumes the unreadable marks are flanking water sigils and opposing pairs of Regions signs.

name: Floating Expansion
description: A fully visible seal drawn in orange on a yellow background, ring closed. A Selection sign sits at the center in place of an element sigil. Four triple-lined Expansion signs surround it at the four intercardinal points, each with its corner pointing outward toward the ring. In the gaps between them, at north, south, east and west, sit four Stability and Level Planes signs drawn as three wavy lines. Small Columns signs sit near the rim on either side of each Stability and Level Planes sign, pointing in toward the center.
justification: No element sigil appears, so the Selection sign at the center limits the spell to the object the seal is drawn on. Expansion is semi-directional, and with its corners pointing outward it makes the target grow rather than shrink. Stability and Level Planes keeps the object balanced on a plane in the air, and the inward-facing Columns signs give that lift a vertical push. Together they enlarge and float only the object bearing the seal.
effect: Makes the object it is drawn on grow to many times its original size and levitate in the air.

name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
description: A fully visible seal in black ink on a white background, with the outer ring closed. A wind sigil, an S-shaped spiral flanked by short dashes on either side, sits at the center and is small relative to the ring. Around it is a single Dancing Puppets sign, drawn as an inner ring with four small circles at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest points. Curved lines cross through those circles and reach outward, and short straight strokes mark the north, south, east and west of the inner ring. No other signs are present.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Dancing Puppets placed around a sigil lets the target's movement be manipulated, and paired with wind it lets objects fly and be thrown about in the air. With no directional signs, the motion has no set direction and behaves erratically.
effect: Sends nearby objects darting into the sky and moving around erratically, with enough force to carry some objects up into the air.

name: Flying Puppet of Diversion
description: A manga panel of a hooded cloak tumbling through the air with speed lines behind it, and a small curly-haired girl below reaching up toward it. A small round object with a few indistinct marks floats beside the cloak, but it is too small to show a ring, sigil, or recognizable sign. No legible seal or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. No sigil or sign can be identified, and the flying cloak is an effect, not a glyph.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Gathering Shadows
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black on a plain background, ring closed. The center holds a Concealment sign, an eight-armed star whose north, east, south, and west arms each end in an eye mark. There is no element sigil. Four Envelopment signs, each a slanted stroke with short hooks at both ends, sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast positions, off the four diagonal arms of the central sign.
justification: The seal has no element sigil. Instead, the Concealment sign takes the center and sets the spell's purpose: hiding a target. The four Envelopment signs make that effect surround whatever the object covers, so the concealment wraps around the target rather than acting on a single point. The balanced placement of four Envelopment signs at the diagonals spreads the effect evenly over the drawn object.
effect: Makes the object it is drawn on absorb all light that strikes it, so it disappears into shadow. Anyone who covers themselves with the object is concealed within the shadows along with it.

name: Grasping Wind
description: A fully visible seal drawn in rough black ink on a white background, with the ring closed. A Wind sigil sits at the center: an S-shaped spiral flanked by short strokes on either side. Four Pulling signs sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast points, each with its arrowhead pointing in toward the sigil along the diagonal. No other signs are visible.
justification: The Wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves existing air. Pulling signs with their arrows pointing inward draw the spell's element toward the seal, so four of them around a Wind sigil pull the surrounding air toward the center from all sides. Because the four signs are evenly spaced, the pull is balanced rather than biased in one direction. Pulling signs set at an angle add a twisting motion, but these appear to point mostly straight inward.
effect: Creates a strong wind current flowing toward the seal, with enough force to pull lighter objects toward it. If the Pulling signs are slanted, the air twists into a vortex that spins objects as they are drawn in.

name: Integration
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a small gap at the bottom. An earth sigil sits at the center. Six Crushing signs surround it, all inverted. One sits at the north point as a W shape and one at the south point as an M shape. The other four are stretched zigzag Crushing signs at the northeast, northwest, southeast and southwest, angled to follow the curve of the ring. No other signs are present.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell acting on solid matter. Crushing is a semi-directional sign, so its direction does not steer the spell, but inverting it reverses its effect. Normal Crushing breaks solids into smaller and smaller pieces. Inverted Crushing does the opposite and pulls crushed material back into its original form. With only inverted Crushing signs around the earth sigil, the whole seal is built to reform matter rather than break it. Because the ring is open, the spell would not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Takes powdered or smashed solid particles within its range and temporarily rearranges them into the shape of the object they came from. This makes an unknown powder easy to identify. When the spell wears off or is removed, the material falls back into its broken state.

name: Inverted Scalewolf Curse
