description: A manga panel set against a scale-like background. One hand holds a pen with its tip pressed to a surface, while a second hand rests flat beside it. Under the pen and fingers are a few ink marks: a small circle near the pen tip and some short curved strokes. Most of the drawing is covered by the hands and pen, so no sigil or sign can be identified. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen.
justification: Nothing to decode. A glyph appears to be present, but the visible strokes are too fragmentary and too hidden to match any sigil or sign.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Inverted Scalewolf Curse
description: A manga panel of a large black scaled wolf leaping forward with its jaws open, while two startled figures in pointed hats watch from the lower left. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere in the panel.
justification: Nothing to decode. The panel shows a creature and onlookers, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Light Beam
description: A fully visible seal drawn in rough black line on a white background. The ring shows a small gap at the bottom, so it is open. A small Light sigil sits at the center, drawn loosely with doubled strokes on its square, diamond, and spokes. Four Columns signs sit at the north, east, south, and west points. Each has its crossbar against the ring and its stem pointing inward, so none is inverted.
justification: The Light sigil makes this a spell that creates and controls light. Its small size relative to the ring points to a modest intensity. Columns makes the magic manifest as a column or beam, and longer signs add force in their direction. The four Columns signs are equal in length and evenly spaced, so they balance one another and the beam rises straight up from the seal rather than leaning to one side. Because the ring is open, the spell would need the gap closed before it activates.
effect: Creates a beam of light shining straight up from the seal. The more precisely the glyphs are drawn, the steadier the beam.

name: Light Tracer
description: A small, fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed and drawn with a rough doubled line. At the center sits a light sigil, a diamond inside a square with short lines extending outward. It is wrapped by a Stretch sign, an arc that curves over the top of the sigil and opens toward the bottom. A single Link sign sits at the north point above the arc. No other signs are visible.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell makes and shapes light. Stretch surrounds the sigil as it is meant to and draws the magic out into a long, flexible ribbon, which turns the light into a thin string. Link identifies objects broken off from the same source and connects them, so the string of light runs between those pieces. The closed ring allows the spell to activate.
effect: When drawn on one fragment of a broken object, the spell sends a string of light from that fragment to every other fragment of the same object, tracing the connection between the pieces.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A small, tilted, dark oval seal drawn in white lines. The center shows a glyph of concentric circles with a dot in the middle, and several short white strokes radiate outward from it toward the ring, with small marks scattered around them. The seal is foreshortened and very small, so none of the surrounding signs can be matched to a named sign. A pale shape overlaps the upper left edge. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told.
justification: The concentric circles with a central dot and the radiating hand-like strokes match the memory erasure sigil and its attached keystones. Those keystones resemble Glaives, which set how deeply magic embeds itself into the flesh. The smaller marks that separate one variant from another are too small to read, so only the core spell can be identified.
effect: Likely erases memories from the target's mind. Variants can wipe the mind entirely, wipe all memory of magic, wipe all memory of a secret or conversation, or wipe all memory of a person. Which variant this is cannot be determined from the image, because the surrounding signs cannot be read.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A manga panel showing a close-up of a girl's face in profile on the left, with a hand reaching in from the right toward her eyes. Between the fingers sits a small dark round shape with a few thin trailing lines below it and some tiny white marks on and around it. The fingers cover most of the shape, and what remains is too small and dark to show a ring, sigil, or any identifiable sign.
justification: A seal appears to be present, but no sigil or sign can be matched, and whether the ring is open or closed cannot be told. There is nothing legible to decode.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Memory Erasure
description: A small manga panel showing a round seal drawn in white lines on a black disk. The ring appears closed. At the center sits a sigil of concentric circles with a dot in the middle. Several branching, hand-like lines spread out from it, mostly toward the south and sides, and resemble Glaives signs. A few small dots are scattered inside the ring. The right edge is clipped by the panel border, and the image is too small to read the finer marks.
justification: The concentric-circle sigil sets the kind of magic, which is not one of the elemental sigils. The branching Glaives-like strokes set how deeply the magic embeds itself into its target. The small dots are additional signs, but they are too small to identify, so the exact variant cannot be read from the visible marks.
effect: Erases memories from the target's mind. Known variants wipe the mind entirely, wipe all memory of magic, wipe memory of a secret or conversation, or wipe all memory of a person. Which variant this is cannot be determined from the image.

name: Mirror Spell
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a clean background. The main ring is closed and has no element sigil at its center, which is left empty. Four smaller closed satellite circles sit at the northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest points, each holding a single tilted Reflection sign. Inside the main ring are four more Reflection signs: upright at north and south, turned sideways at east and west. At the four cardinal points the ring bulges into bracket-shaped signs that match Projection, flanked by partial-circle and line shapes. Angled lines from those shapes run out to connect each satellite circle to the main ring.
justification: With no sigil, the seal is driven entirely by its signs. Eight Reflection signs, four inside the ring and one in each satellite, make targeting a reflected image the core of the spell. The four Projection signs send that captured image outward. The linking lines tie the satellite Reflection signs into the main ring, so the reflections they capture feed the projection.
effect: Reflects whatever is looking at the seal by capturing its image and projecting it outward. When linked with a spell that gathers shadows, it lets the bearer take on the appearance of any animal that gazes at them. Its full effect on its own is not known.

name: Pegasus Carriage Spell
description: A fully visible, highly complex seal drawn in black line on a white background, with an outer ring and an inner ring, both closed. The band between the two rings is filled with a repeating chain of small curled Wind signs. Just inside the inner ring, many Columns signs, some single and some doubled, line the edge pointing inward. Four smaller closed circles sit at the north, south, east, and west. The north and south circles each hold a three-armed whorl sigil, a variant of the wind sigil, ringed by three Columns signs. The east and west circles each hold a wind-like S-shaped sigil with mirrored markings, surrounded by small signs that resemble Levitation and Aeriforms Defined. Small curled signs sit in the open space between the four circles. At the center is a three-lined Stability and Level Planes sign.
justification: The four sub-circles each contain a wind-family sigil, so the whole seal works with air. The north and south whorl sigils are Whorling Wind, which moves air by rotating it, and their three Columns signs push that motion in a set direction. The east and west sigils are Wind Underfoot, which supports solid objects in the air, and the Levitation and Aeriforms Defined signs around them add lift. The central Stability and Level Planes sign keeps the target balanced on a level plane like a float on water. The many Columns signs along the inner ring direct the overall force, and the outer band of Wind signs adds further wind behavior. The seal is mirrored top to bottom and left to right, so the effect is evenly balanced.
effect: A wind spell that keeps a carriage aloft and lets it fly while being pulled through the air. It holds the carriage level and stable throughout the flight.

name: Pegasus Carriage Spell
description: A manga panel showing the lower part of a very large seal. The top of the seal runs past the frame, and a hand and a figure holding a pen cover the bottom center and right, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen. The outer edge is a band between two concentric rings, filled with a repeating row of small curled signs that match the Sign of Wind. Just inside it, a dense row of Columns signs lines the inner ring all the way around the visible arc. Toward the middle sits a small circle holding a three-armed spiral sigil in the style of a whorling wind sigil, with small Columns signs set around it. To its left is an S-shaped spiral resembling the wind sigil, also with short Columns-like marks nearby. Further curls on the right are partly hidden under hatching. The middle of the seal is cut off, so the full set of sigils and any central signs cannot be read.
justification: The visible sigils are all wind variants, so this is a wind spell. The three-armed spiral reads as Whorling Wind, which moves air by rotation. The S-shaped spiral reads as a wind sigil of the Wind Underfoot kind, which supports solid objects in the air. The Columns signs around the inner sigil and along the inner ring direct that air in a set direction. The Sign of Wind repeated around the outer band adds a further wind modifier whose exact role is unclear. The many sigils and the evenly spaced rows of signs suggest a symmetric seal. This reading assumes the hidden half mirrors the visible half, with a second whorling sigil and a second wind-type sigil.
effect: Moves and directs air beneath a large object to keep it aloft and flying while it is pulled along. This assumes the parts of the seal that are cut off or covered mirror the visible part.

name: Petrification
description: A manga panel of a figure turned to jagged, rock-like material, one arm raised and holding a small object aloft, surrounded by crystalline spikes. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible, and the held object shows no readable markings.
justification: Nothing to decode. The stone-like figure and spikes are an effect, not a glyph.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image because no glyph is visible.

name: Phantasmal Fireball
description: A manga panel showing a fully visible seal against grey shaded tone, with the ring closed. A large triangle is inscribed inside the ring, its three points touching or nearly touching it. A small filled square sits at each of the triangle's vertices. A fire sigil, small relative to the ring, sits at the center inside the large triangle. Three branching, feather-like signs sit in the spaces between the triangle and the ring, one at the north and one each at the southwest and southeast. None of them clearly matches a known sign. Three small round knobs are attached to the outside of the ring, at the northwest, northeast and south. A few small strokes near the triangle's edges are too small to read.
justification: The fire sigil sets the spell as fire magic, and its small size points to a gentle intensity. The large triangle with squares at its vertices, the three matching branching signs and the three outer knobs are arranged with threefold symmetry around the sigil. None of these match a known sign, so their exact roles cannot be decoded sign by sign. Because they repeat evenly, they act on the flame the same way on every side rather than pushing it in one direction, which fits a steady, contained flame.
effect: Creates a flame that gives off light but no heat. The flame can be touched without injury, which makes it useful as a safe light source and for scaring off beasts.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a plain background, ring closed. A fire sigil sits at the center, drawn fairly large relative to the ring. Four Levitation signs are placed at the northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast points, evenly spaced, with their arrowheads pointing inward toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so the spell creates and controls flame, and its fairly large size gives a strong flame. Levitation floats the magic above the seal, and when the signs are balanced the result tends to take the shape of a sphere. Four equal signs evenly placed around the sigil are balanced, so the flame forms a floating ball. The length of the Levitation signs sets how much weight the spell can carry.
effect: Creates a ball of fire that floats above the seal and also lifts any object that is not too heavy placed directly above it.

name: Pyreball Seal
description: A manga panel. A sheet of paper lies on a table with a small oval seal drawn on it, seen at a steep angle. The ring appears closed, though a wisp rising from its upper edge makes the top hard to read. Inside are a small central mark and four tiny marks at the north, south, east, and west points. At this size they look like short arrow-like strokes, possibly Levitation signs, but neither the central sigil nor the signs can be clearly identified.
justification: The layout of one central glyph with four matching signs at the cardinal points fits a balanced seal, but the strokes are too small to confirm. If the center is a fire sigil and the four signs are Levitation, the fire sigil would set the element and the balanced Levitation signs would lift the result above the seal.
effect: The effect cannot be fully confirmed from the image. If the center is a fire sigil ringed by Levitation signs, the spell creates a ball of fire that levitates above the seal and can lift light objects held directly above it.

name: Rainbringer Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal in black ink on a white background, ring closed. A large Rain sign fills most of the ring: a square with inward-curving sides and pointed corners, with three parallel lines crossing each of its four sides at north, east, south, and west. A water sigil sits in the empty space at the center of the Rain sign, drawn turned on its side so the S-curve runs roughly horizontally with one teardrop above it and one below. No other signs are present.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water, and its large size within the ring gives a fairly strong effect. Rain is a sign that surrounds a central sigil and summons the target material, here water, to fall within its area. The Rain sign is drawn the normal way, not flipped inside-out, so it brings water down rather than pushing it away. The rotation of the sigil does not change its meaning, and with the ring closed the spell is active.
effect: Generates a shower of rain that falls over the seal's area.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal in black line work on a plain background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center. A small fire sigil marks the north point and another marks the south point, both drawn compactly with their triangles oriented toward the center. A Crosshair sign sits at the east point and another at the west point, each a long vertical stroke crossed by short horizontal ends.
justification: The central water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. The two small fire sigils add a second, heat-based element above and below it; their small size relative to the ring keeps that effect mild. The two Crosshair signs direct the seal's magic at whatever their short ends point toward, so the combined water and fire magic is aimed at the water around the seal rather than producing new water.
effect: Creates a water-repellent area, forming a bubble devoid of water within the spell's radius. Whether it does this by repelling the water or by drying it away is not known.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open with a small gap at the bottom. At the center is a horizontal double spiral, a variant of the wind sigil drawn without its side strokes. North of it is a modified fire sigil: an upright triangle with two lines crossing over it in an X. South is a matching modified fire sigil, inverted so the triangle points downward. One Crosshair sign sits at the east point and one at the west point, each with its short ends facing the ring and the center.
justification: The central wind-variant sigil sets the spell as air magic. It is the largest glyph in the ring, so it drives the main effect. The two modified fire sigils above and below add heat. One is inverted, which matches the drying arrangement of this seal. The two Crosshair signs aim the magic at whatever their short ends point toward, which confines the effect to the area around the seal. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn.
effect: Clears water from the space around the seal. It either repels water to leave a bubble free of water within its radius, or, with the inverted fire sigils, dries things off and warms them up. The ring must be closed for the spell to activate.

name: Rainflinger
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds a horizontal double spiral, an S-shaped curl that reads as a variant of the wind sigil, drawn without the side ticks of the base wind sigil. At the north point sits a fire-like glyph: a triangle pointing down toward the center, with two diagonal strokes crossing over it in an X. At the south point sits a matching fire-like glyph, a triangle pointing up toward the center with its own crossing strokes. A Crosshair sign sits at the east point and another at the west point. The seal is symmetric north to south and east to west, with no other signs.
justification: The wind-variant sigil at the center sets the base magic as air. The two modified fire glyphs add heat to that air. Both point inward, so the heat acts within the seal. The two Crosshair signs direct the effect onto whatever their shorter ends point at, which keeps it focused on a defined area around the seal. Together these produce warm, moving air acting on a set area, which pushes water out of that space. A nearly identical form with inverted fire glyphs and a broken line through each triangle dries and warms instead. The strokes here are too small to tell those two forms apart with certainty.
effect: Creates a water-repellent area that forms a bubble free of water within the spell's radius. The closely related drying form instead dries off objects and warms them up.

name: Repetition Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, drawn as two concentric rings, both closed, forming a band around an empty center. No sigil sits in the middle. Four Repetition signs sit on the band at the north, east, south and west points. In each of the four quadrants between them is a group of three signs: a Convergence triangle pointing inward toward the center, flanked on each side by a Columns sign with its crossbar toward the outer ring. That makes four Repetition, four Convergence and eight Columns signs in all.
justification: Repetition can stand in for a sigil and is the basis of the seal; it continually resets whatever the spell affects to the state it had when the spell first touched it. The Columns signs set an area of effect in the shape of a column, and their count raises the range. The inward-pointing Convergence signs focus the magic toward a single point and can make loose material pack tightly together. Spread evenly around the band, these balanced signs apply the reset uniformly to whatever lies within the inner ring.
effect: Reverts the affected object to its original form, making it like new. Rotten food becomes fresh, dirty clothing becomes new and clean, and any later change, such as added embroidery, is undone.

name: Reverse Time
description: A manga panel of an open book held in a hand. On the right page is a large circular seal with the ring closed, filled with straight lines that form overlapping triangles and other geometric shapes in a star-like arrangement. There is no recognizable element sigil at the center. Fingers cross the lower right part of the seal and hide some lines, and the line work is too small to separate into individual named signs. The left page shows several smaller glyphs: one resembling a Repetition sign, a swirl shape, and a ringed circular pattern. These are too small to read in detail.
justification: No element sigil can be identified, so the seal does not take its behavior from a primary sigil. Its structure of straight lines forming geometric shapes in a star-like layout matches the family of time-reversal seals. These are related to Repetition, which resets objects to an earlier state, but they work without the Repetition sigil. The individual signs cannot be decoded at this size, and the covered portion is assumed to mirror the visible geometric pattern.
effect: Reverses time on the target to undo wear and other damage, for up to one day. When that time runs out, the glyph vanishes and the target returns to the state it would have without the spell. The glyph can be reapplied to repeat the effect. This reading assumes the hidden part of the seal follows the same symmetric geometric pattern.

name: Rising Platform of Water
description: A fully visible, roughly drawn seal on a plain background, ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, with its two droplets flanking the central curve. Eight signs surround it in alternating order. Four Levitation signs sit at about the north, east, south and west points, each turned on its side so the arrow lies roughly sideways rather than pointing straight at the center. Four Columns signs sit between them at the intercardinal points, each oriented outward from the sigil.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. The outward Columns signs give it a columnar area of effect, and because there are four balanced around the ring, the column forms evenly over the seal instead of leaning to one side. The four sideways Levitation signs are also balanced, so their lifting effect acts straight up on whatever the seal is drawn on rather than carrying it in one direction. Together the signs form a rising pillar of water that carries its object upward.
effect: Generates an upward surge of water in a column that lifts the object the seal is drawn on straight up into the air, acting as a rising platform.

name: Rising Wave
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring open at the bottom. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn at moderate size relative to the ring. A ring of Columns signs runs around the inside edge, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem toward the center. Small V-shaped Regions signs alternate with the Columns across the upper half only. The lower Columns stand alone, and the space around the gap at the bottom is empty. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell. Columns signs make the magic manifest as a column and drive it with force, and their number raises the amount of water produced. Regions signs set where magic manifests relative to the seal. Because they appear only on the upper half, the surge is biased toward that side, so the column of water leans and travels at an angle rather than straight up. The ring must be closed before the spell will activate.
effect: Creates a powerful surge of water that rises diagonally upward, strong enough to launch the caster into the air.

name: Sand Bridge
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on a round disc, seen at a steep angle and drawn in rough, sketchy ink. The outer ring appears closed, with a narrow outer band of small marks too tiny to identify. A small inner ring at the center holds a sigil that is too small and foreshortened to name. Around it radiate several signs shaped like two small circles joined by a line, which match Solidification. They are clearest on the upper left and lower side. Other short, branching signs sit on the right side, but they are too blurred to match. The upper right edge of the disc runs off the panel, and the far side is compressed by the angle.
justification: The Solidification signs make the material the seal controls more solid. Grouped around the center, they suggest a spell that forms loose material into a firm structure. The central sigil cannot be read, so the element cannot be confirmed from the image. The remaining signs are too blurred to say how the structure is shaped or held in place.
effect: Raises loose earth and sand into a solid temporary bridge that can be crossed until a permanent one is built. Only the hardening part of this can be read from the visible Solidification signs. The rest is assumed from the seal being a sand bridge, since the sigil and most signs are not legible.

name: Sand Bridge
description: A manga panel showing a large arched bridge of sand spanning a river, seen from above, with a girl in the foreground looking up at it in excitement. Two blank rectangular boxes sit in the upper part of the panel. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible anywhere.
justification: Nothing to decode. The bridge is the result of a spell, not a glyph, and no part of a seal appears in the image.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image, since no glyph is visible.

name: Sealchair Glyph
description: A manga panel showing a large compound seal drawn on a flat wooden surface between two curved, leg-like shapes. At the center is an oval main ring that appears closed. Inside it sits a dense central glyph of crossing strokes, flanked by several smaller enclosed rings packed with clustered marks. Lines run outward from the main ring to satellite circles: larger ones at the upper left, upper right, left and right, and several small ones along the edges. The upper satellites are cut off by the top of the frame. The left and right satellites are partly hidden behind the curved legs. Every sign, inside the main ring and in the satellites, is too small and too blurred by screentone to match to a known sign or sigil.
justification: Nothing can be decoded. No sigil can be identified, so the element is unknown, and no individual sign is legible enough to name. That leaves no modifiers to combine. The layout does show a main seal linked to multiple satellite seals, but what each part contributes cannot be read.
effect: The signs and sigils are not readable, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Serpent's Bed of Sand
description: A rough ink sketch of a fully visible compound seal on a plain background, outer ring closed. A wide outer band runs between two concentric rings and holds two kinds of marks in alternation. One is a spiral eye-like glyph matching Repetition, which appears about six times around the band. The other is a group of a Columns sign, an inward-pointing Convergence triangle, and a second Columns sign, which appears about five times, each group turned to follow the band. Inside the inner ring is a central square holding a circle with a four-lobed Billow shape. Around it sit several small closed seals, about five, each with a tiny sigil and signs that are too small to read individually. A few stray ink marks surround the drawing.
justification: The outer band of Repetition glyphs with paired Columns and Convergence is a repetition seal. It keeps resetting whatever it affects to its original state, while Convergence packs loose particles tightly together. Billow sits at the center in place of a sigil and turns available material into a fluffy cloud. The small ring seals around it are assumed to be earth seals that pair an earth sigil with Crushing and Columns to grind stone into sand, though their contents cannot be confirmed at this resolution. Together, the parts crush stone into sand, gather it, billow it into a cloud, compact it so it can bear weight, and keep it from falling apart.
effect: Creates a large, fluffy cloud made of sand that is firm and stable enough to hold up a dragon. The repeating layer continually restores the cloud to its original shape.

name: Skysoaring Seal
description: A fully visible hand-drawn seal on a clean background, ring closed. A wind sigil with its short side strokes sits in the lower part of the ring, toward the south, rather than at the center. A single elongated Levitation sign runs from the north edge of the ring down to just above the sigil, its crossbar at the north and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a wind spell that moves air. Levitation is a directional sign, so its angle and length steer where the spell acts. Its length also sets how far the target travels, how much weight it carries, and how fast it moves. Here it is stretched across nearly the whole ring along a single axis. With only one Levitation sign and nothing to balance it, the moving air is pushed one way along that axis instead of holding the target in place.
effect: Produces a strong thrust of moving air in one direction along the line of the Levitation sign. When drawn large enough on a big surface such as a sail, it can make that object fly.

name: Skysoaring Seal
description: A manga two-page spread. On the left, large spherical rocks float above a wide landscape, with inset panels of a girl looking upward and a girl clinging to a rope-lashed pole. On the right, a figure hangs from a sail on a pole above a boat that leaps out of splashing water, with large black bars behind it and a small inset showing the sail and the boat. The sails show only plain tone, with no ring, sigil, or sign visible.
justification: There is nothing to decode. The flying sail and the leaping boat are effects, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Snugstone Spell
description: A close-up manga panel of an oval stone with a seal drawn on it. Several dark cracks run across the stone, cutting through the ring and the glyphs. A fire sigil sits at the center, split by a crack. An inverted Columns sign, crossbar toward the center, sits at the south point, and a matching inverted Columns sign is visible at the east point. Four curled, crescent-shaped signs sit at the intercardinal points. The north and west points are obscured by the cracks and dark lines, so any signs there cannot be read. The inner ring line is broken by the cracks, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be confirmed.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as fire. Columns inverted around the sigil spread their effect horizontally outward instead of beaming it upward, behaving much like Dispersion. The curled signs at the intercardinal points are a radial modifier that tempers the fire's output, turning flame into gentle heat. Assuming the hidden north and west points mirror the visible inverted Columns, the seal pushes mild heat evenly out on all sides.
effect: Radiates a steady, gentle warmth outward in all directions without producing any flame. This assumes the obscured north and west signs match the visible inverted Columns.

name: Spell of Reduction
description: A manga panel showing the edge of a box or lid with a hand beneath it. A fragment of a seal runs along the edge. A curved stroke, a short vertical line, a small Diamond sign, and nested angle marks resembling one corner of an Expansion sign are visible. The ring and the rest of the seal are cut off by the edge of the box and the panel framing, so it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed, and no sigil can be confirmed.
justification: The Diamond sign is identifiable, and the nested angles match part of an Expansion sign. The curved stroke may belong to a central Repetition glyph, but too little is visible to confirm it. Expansion is semi-directional: corners pointing outward make the target grow, and corners pointing inward (inverted) make it shrink. Diamond likely restricts the effect to objects inside the container the seal is drawn on, not the container itself. The visible angles are too fragmentary to show which way they face.
effect: Likely shrinks items placed inside the container to far below their normal size. This assumes the hidden part of the seal holds inverted Expansion signs around a central glyph, with Diamond signs in the gaps, mirroring the visible fragment.

name: Spike
description: A manga panel of a crouching figure behind a large curved spray of debris, with several thick spikes flying through the air and one embedded in the ground. No ring, sigil, or sign is visible.
justification: Nothing to decode. The spikes and spray are an effect, not a glyph.
effect: No glyph is visible, so the effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Sylph Shoes Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a plain background, ring closed. The center holds a large Wind Underfoot sigil, a variant of the wind sigil: an S-shaped double spiral flanked by curved strokes on both sides. Around it, a single band of signs runs inside the ring, alternating between Convergence triangles and Levitation arrows, roughly eight of each. The triangles have one point aimed inward, and the arrowheads also point toward the center.
justification: The Wind Underfoot sigil makes this wind magic of the kind that supports solid objects in the air, and its large size relative to the ring gives a strong effect. Levitation lifts the target into the air, and its even, balanced spacing keeps the lift steady on all sides. Convergence focuses the magic about a single point, so the lift stays centered under the target instead of spreading out. With every sign evenly spaced and pointing inward, the seal pushes no particular way and the target is held aloft.
effect: Lets the wearer float and fly above the ground. The seal is drawn in two halves that only form a closed ring, and so only activate, when the two halves are brought together.

name: Twin Bottle's Spell
description: A manga panel showing the curved, dark surface of a bottle. A small oval seal is drawn on it, seen at an angle, with its ring closed and a bright glow radiating around it. Faint marks inside the ring, including a cross-like shape near the center, can be made out, but the glow, the screentone, and the small scale blur every line. No sigil or sign can be matched to a known form.
justification: Nothing to decode. The seal is present, but its sigil and signs are too small and too washed out by the glow to identify. No element or modifier can be read.
effect: The effect cannot be determined from the image.

name: Wall Breaker Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal on a plain background. The ring is open, with a small gap at the bottom. An earth sigil sits at the center. One Columns sign sits at the west point and one at the east point, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing toward the sigil. One Crushing sign sits at the north point and one at the south point, both facing the normal way rather than inverted.
justification: The earth sigil makes this an earth spell that acts on solid matter such as stone, wood, and soil. Normal Crushing signs break the target into smaller and smaller pieces until it is a powder; the larger the signs, the finer the result. The paired Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect and push it in a set direction, driving the crushing through the material. Because the ring is open, the spell is drawn but not yet active; closing the ring would cast it.
effect: Breaks through the solid material it is drawn on and reduces it to dust or sand.

name: Water Bolt
description: A manga page. The top panel shows part of a large seal drawn on the ground. The curve of its ring runs along the left side, and the rest is cut off by the panel borders, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen. Across the middle runs a row of at least three Piercing signs, each a straight line with a diamond along it. Near them are a few small chevron marks that look like Regions signs, though their exact direction is hard to read. Splashing water and a foot pressing down on the seal hide much of the interior. No sigil can be identified in the visible area. The bottom panel shows a figure holding a staff, with speed lines and no glyph.
justification: Several Piercing signs in a row make the magic manifest as projectiles, and their number sets how many. Regions signs that all point the same way send that magic in one direction. Together they describe a row of projectiles fired one way. The sigil that would set the element is not visible, so the element cannot be confirmed from what is shown.
effect: Likely shoots a row of water bolts straight ahead, with more Piercing signs producing more bolts, and works best when drawn large. This assumes the hidden part of the seal holds a water sigil, which cannot be seen here.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A manga panel showing an oval seal drawn on a surface, ring closed and fully in frame, with fingers or tool tips pressing in at the east and west edges. A water sigil sits at the center. Beside it on the east and west sit tall stacked signs that resemble Mimicry, though their outer parts are partly covered where the hands overlap. Along the north is a row of small signs that look like Columns with a peaked mark among them, too small and rough to identify with certainty. Along the south is a row of alternating straight lines and V-shaped marks that resemble Regions signs pointing toward the center.
justification: The water sigil sets the element as water. The Mimicry-like signs make the magic imitate the movements of a creature form. The marks in the north row likely include the sign that shapes the water. The Regions-like V marks control where the magic manifests relative to the ring. Because the north row is not clearly legible, the shaping sign cannot be confirmed.
effect: Creates a horse made of water that moves like a real horse and can be used to pull a vehicle. This assumes the illegible north row holds the horse-shaping sign.

name: Water Pen
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, drawn in black line. A water sigil sits at the center. A Holding sign wraps around it, with one curved bracket on the east and one on the west, each ending in a dot at the bottom. At the north point is a joined figure that reads as a Dispersion sign with two Columns signs projecting sideways from either end, forming an H-like shape. At the south point is a Pointing sign, a triangle with a crossbar flanked by two curled strokes.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the seal acts on water. Holding keeps that water in the shape the seal defines while still letting it move. Pointing tapers the water into a cone or blade. The Columns and Dispersion signs at the north set where the shaped water manifests and let its magic seep outward from the formed body rather than shooting off as a beam.
effect: Creates a dagger-shaped glob of water that hovers below the seal at an angle. Conjuring ink can be poured into the dagger to saturate it, turning it into a pen that can draw very large seals on almost any surface.

name: Watershot Seal
description: A fully visible, hand-drawn seal with the ring closed. A water sigil sits at the center, drawn small relative to the ring. Around the inside of the ring sit about seven small Columns signs, each with its bar toward the ring and its stem toward the center: one at north, one at each upper diagonal, and others down the east and west sides. At the south point a single larger Columns sign stretches from just below the sigil to the ring, noticeably longer than the others.
justification: The water sigil makes this a water spell, and its small size keeps the effect modest. Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area of effect and push it in a given direction. More Columns signs raise the range or amount of water produced. When all are balanced and of equal length, the water rises straight up from the seal. A longer Columns sign adds pressure in its direction, so the extended southern sign likely tilts or strengthens the stream on that side.
effect: Creates a stream of water that shoots out from the seal, straight up when the Columns signs are balanced. The longer southern sign likely adds extra push on that side.

name: Wind Wall
description: A manga panel with part of a seal visible. A large white rounded shape covers the top of the seal, and vertical lines cut across the right side, so the seal is only partly visible and it cannot be seen whether the ring is open or closed. Near the center is a spiral stroke that matches part of a wind sigil, with a small dot beside it. About six small triangles that match Convergence signs are scattered across the upper left. A curved band with small tick marks along its edges arcs around the lower side of the sigil. Below the band, a row of four or five Columns signs runs along the bottom edge. They are drawn as T shapes, with the bar toward the center and the stem toward the ring, which is the inverted orientation. The upper and right parts of the seal are hidden.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element as moving air. The row of inverted Columns signs makes the magic spread outward horizontally, in a band, rather than rise as a beam. The Convergence signs on the opposite side focus and compact the magic about a point, which keeps the air dense and holds it in shape. The ticked arc around the sigil on the Columns side appears to outline the curve along which the air manifests. Together these signs form a curved, dense barrier of air.
effect: Creates a circular wall of air that is difficult for objects or people to pass through, so it can be used to contain people or animals. This reading assumes the hidden top and right parts follow the arrangement visible here.

name: Windowway Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, made of three closed concentric circles that form two narrow bands, so the ring is closed. The outer band is filled all the way around with small zigzag, lightning bolt-shaped marks set side by side. The inner band is filled all the way around with chevrons that resemble Regions signs, all pointing the same way around the circle in a clockwise direction. The large central area is empty, with no sigil and no other signs inside it.
justification: The two bands of identical, repeated marks lining the seal like extra rings match the Windows sign. Windows does not sit beside a sigil like a conventional sign. Instead it wraps the seal in a band of simple repeated markings, and its variants differ in their mark shapes, which fits the zigzag band here. The inner chevrons look like directional Regions-style signs and are all angled the same way, which suggests they set a flow around the ring. The seal has no element sigil and no location symbol in the center, so it relies entirely on these bands to work.
effect: Opens a gateway between two distant locations, letting one pass from one place to the other. It only functions as part of a matched pair, with each seal varied so that it links only to its own partner.

name: Ancient Labyrinth Spell
description: A large seal is drawn in white over a scaled, winding path. Its outer boundary is a dotted line, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be judged, and a row of short T-shaped ticks resembling Columns signs runs along its lower edge. Inside, a band alternates small chevrons resembling Regions signs with figure-like glyphs made of circles, crossbars and loops. A second, tighter ring of similar figure-like glyphs surrounds a central circle. The center is washed out by a bright glow, and the path is drawn across it, so no sigil can be seen there. Dense wavy lines rise from the top of the seal like a canopy.
justification: Most glyphs match no known sign. As a guess, the figure-like glyphs are closest to Mimicry, which guides or imitates movement. The chevrons read as Regions, which set where magic manifests relative to the ring. The T-shaped ticks read as Columns, which push force in a set direction. Read together, the seal would confine its effect to a defined area and force movement within it along fixed directions. Without a visible sigil the element cannot be confirmed, and the hidden center may hold signs that change this reading.
effect: Manipulates gravity so that a person can stand upright only along a designated winding path. Stepping off the path, or onto a section whose seal has crumbled, flings the person back to the start of the path.

name: Ancient Light Beacon
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The outer band holds eight Convergence triangles, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point, each with a point aimed inward. Between each pair of triangles sits a three-pronged sign, eight in all. Each has a long stalk aimed toward the center and two curved side prongs. They most resemble Glaives, or possibly Stillness. An inner ring of eight glyphs circles the center. Each is a square and a diamond nested together with a dot in the middle, like a Light sigil without its outer spokes. At the cardinal points the diamond sits inside the square, and at the intercardinal points the square sits inside the diamond. Curved strokes resembling Launch signs join neighboring glyphs into a continuous ring. The center holds a sigil that matches no known glyph: a tall looping oval containing two small circles, flanked by two hooked curves.
justification: The eight nested square-and-diamond glyphs read as variants of the Light sigil, so the spell works with light. The Launch-like connectors between them would generate that light as a short, powerful burst in the direction they point. The inward-pointing Convergence triangles focus the magic down to a single point. Together these suggest a narrow, concentrated beam. The pronged signs are a guess as Glaives or Stillness. Read as Stillness, they would hold the effect fixed in one place, which fits a stationary beacon. The central sigil is unknown. Its closest match is the Water sigil, because of its central curved stroke flanked by side elements, but that reading is a guess. Its role cannot be confirmed, and it may add an effect that cannot be read here.
effect: Presumably creates a column of light, focused to a point and sent upward as a strong burst.

name: Anicent Flames
description: A manga panel of a large billowing cloud of smoke and flame rising from a seal drawn flat on a surface. The seal is seen at an angle as an ellipse, with the ring closed and fully visible below the smoke. The center glyph is a short vertical line flanked by two dots, with an inward-pointing chevron on each side. Around it are four circled glyphs at the cardinal points: a circle crossed by a slash at the north, a circle holding a triangle with a crossbar at the south, and circles with angled marks inside at the east and west. Four small Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, and a few tiny tick-like marks sit near the lower Columns. The glyphs are small but legible.
justification: No standard element sigil is visible. The center glyph most resembles the Cooling sign, a vertical line between dots, with added chevrons; this reading is a guess, and the glyph likely acts as a variant sigil setting the spell's element. The north circle resembles Orb, which would gather the magic into a rounded space above the seal. The south circle resembles a circled Strengthening, which would intensify the effect. The east and west circles hold marks close to Regions, which would keep the magic over the seal. The four Columns signs send the magic upward in a column. Since they are balanced, the effect rises straight up rather than leaning in any direction.
effect: Creates a small fire that rises from the seal and burns like an ordinary fire spell.

name: Beastwarding Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. At the center sits a tall glyph that matches no known sigil: a vertical stem carrying two stacked upward chevrons, capped above and below by bracket shapes that hook inward, like a Projection sign and its mirror. A Light sigil sits at the east point and another at the west point. At the north and south points sits a matching pair of glyphs, each a diamond crossed by two curved strokes that bow toward each other. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, each with its bar toward the center and its stem pointing outward.
justification: The two Light sigils set light as the element. Their size and the open space around them suggest moderate intensity. The four Columns signs are balanced on all sides, so the light is pushed out evenly in every direction rather than toward one side. The central glyph is closest to Gathering because of its stacked chevrons on a stem, though this is a guess. Read that way, it draws in surrounding material to keep the spell fed, and its bracket caps would project that effect outward. The north and south glyphs are closest to the Diamond sign with added curves, also a guess. Read as Diamond, they keep the effect acting on things around the seal rather than on the object carrying it.
effect: Repels animals from the surrounding area. It most likely works by casting light outward in all directions, although whether it relies on light, smell, or sound is not settled.

name: Beldaruit's Illusion Cloak Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the north sits a wind sigil variant: an S-curve with three short strokes on each side instead of two. Below it, three Columns signs curve along each side, six in all, with their stems pointing outward to the upper left and upper right. A horizontal Envelopment sign sits at the west point and another at the east point. At the center is a figure-like glyph: a small circle on a stem that splits into two curved arms. It is flanked by two diamond shapes, each with a dot inside and a horizontal bar across its top point, and each with a single dot below it. Toward the southwest and southeast are sets of three parallel diagonal strokes. A lower row holds a dot, an arrow pointing inward, an eight-spoked asterisk at the center, a second arrow pointing inward from the east, and another dot. At the south, a double arch of two concentric half-circles sits on a baseline. A long diagonal line crosses this arch and runs down to meet the ring at the lower right.
justification: The wind sigil variant sets the element, so the spell moves and shapes air and airborne matter such as smoke. Its small size relative to the ring points to a gentle, controlled effect. The six Columns signs pointing outward push that air away from the center. The Envelopment signs at the sides make the effect wrap around and surround the target. The central figure-like glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Dancing Puppets, so as a guess it lets the shaped material be moved and posed freely. The dotted diamonds are closest to Diamond, a guess, which would limit the effect to what surrounds the bearer rather than the bearer itself. The triple strokes are closest to Detection, also a guess. The inward arrows act like Regions, keeping the magic gathered toward the center around the asterisk. The asterisk resembles the core of Concealment without its eye marks, so as a guess it hides what lies beneath. The double arch at the south is closest to Binding, a guess, which would hold the shaped material together as a single unit. Together these suggest air that is gathered, wrapped around a person and held in a set shape that hides what is underneath.
effect: Sculpts smoke into the illusion of an apprentice's cloak and cap, wrapped around the wearer.

name: Counterclock
description: A manga panel of a figure pulling a robe open to show a seal drawn on the chest. The ring looks closed where it can be seen, but both hands grip the robe over its left and right edges and cover part of the rim and outer markings. Inside the ring there is no recognizable element sigil. Instead, straight lines form a large six-pointed star, with smaller nested polygons and a second, smaller star at the center. Outside the ring, small branch-like marks sit above, to the sides, and below, and some trail down the chest. A few resemble Gathering signs and others look like Aeriforms Defined, but they are small and partly hidden.
justification: No sigil from the elemental families is present, so the element is not set by a central glyph. The six-pointed star matches no known sign. The closest reading is two overlapping Convergence triangles, one pointing inward and one outward, but this is a guess. Read that way, the opposed triangles would focus the magic on the target and also act against its current state, which fits a reversal effect. The outer marks, if they are Gathering signs, would draw in what the spell needs from its surroundings, though this is also uncertain. The hidden edges under the hands may hold more signs that cannot be read.
effect: Reverses time on the target, undoing wear and other damage. The effect lasts at most a day. When it expires, the spell vanishes and the target returns to the state it was in before the spell was cast, unless the seal is drawn again.

name: Dragon Smokesculpture
description: A manga panel showing a large seal drawn across a broad surface. One hand rests flat on the lower left, and a second hand holds a pen at the right, mid-stroke. No ring edge is visible, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be seen, and the seal is only partly visible because the panel crops it on every side. Many small Columns signs, mostly upright with some inverted, run in curving rows on both sides of a vertical central axis. At the top of the axis is a tall, symmetric loop flanked by drop-like strokes. Below it, a vertical line carries several downward chevrons like stacked Pulling arrows, followed by a figure with a small circle on a stem crossed by short bars. Near the bottom, a horizontal shaft with chevrons pointing left looks like a Levitation or Pulling sign turned sideways. Small asterisk-like marks sit at the upper left and upper right, and a few wavy dotted strokes lie right of center. Parts of the lower half are hidden under the hands and fingers.
justification: The dense rows of Columns signs set the direction and range of the magic, and their large number points to a wide area of effect, with the inverted ones spreading part of it sideways. The sideways chevron shaft is closest to Levitation, which would keep the result floating and moving through the air. This reading is a guess. The circle-on-stem figure is closest to Mimicry, also a guess, which would make the magic copy the movements of a shaped form. The drop-flanked loop at the top only loosely resembles a water sigil, and no element sigil can be confirmed. Because the hands and the panel edges hide parts of the seal, the full combination cannot be read.
effect: Creates a dragon out of smoke that can fly through the air and roar. The visible Columns, Levitation-like, and Mimicry-like signs are consistent with this, but the element sigil and the hidden portions cannot be confirmed from what is shown.

name: Fish Guidance
description: A manga panel showing a seal whose bottom edge is cut off by the panel border, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed. A small inner ring sits at the center and holds a sigil that matches neither a primary element nor a light sigil. It is drawn as a pointed, triangular shape with an inner stroke. Two Columns signs are visible: one at the upper left, angled with its stem running toward the inner ring, and one at the east. Two Crosshair signs sit near the north and the west. Two Stability and Level Planes signs appear as wavy lines, one at the northeast and a partly visible one at the southwest. Two looped, figure-like glyphs resembling an abstract fish sit at the north and the southwest. A branched, trident-like glyph with several prongs sits at the southeast. Any signs along the bottom are cut off.
justification: The central sigil is the Guidance sigil, which draws objects to the seal that match the parameters set by the other glyphs. The fish-like figures read as decorative sigils, which limit a spell to things shaped by the same design. Paired with the Crosshairs, whose short ends aim the effect at a target, they pick out water shaped like fish. The Columns direct the movement along a set path. The Stability and Level Planes keep the guided objects balanced on a level plane in the air. The branched glyph at the southeast matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Glaives, though this is a guess. Read that way, it would set how firmly the guidance takes hold of its target. Its many prongs could also mark a second decorative shape.
effect: Draws floating water sculptures shaped like fish and birds toward the seal and guides them there through the air. This assumes the cut-off bottom of the seal holds nothing that changes the effect.

name: Flowers of Light
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A Light sigil sits at the center, a square overlaid with a diamond and short cross lines, with a dot at its middle. It is enclosed by a pentagon, and a long straight spoke runs from each of the pentagon's five corners out toward the ring: north, east-northeast, southeast, southwest and west-northwest. In each of the five gaps between the spokes sits an identical small glyph: a straight line pointing inward toward the pentagon, topped by two curling hooks that branch to either side like a sprouting stem. These sit at the northwest, northeast, west-southwest, east-southeast and south positions. None of these five glyphs matches a named sign.
justification: The Light sigil sets the element as light, which falls under fire magic. The pentagon with five radiating spokes reads as the decorative sigil for flowers, which gives the spell's magic the rough shape of a flower. Decorative sigils take up a large part of the seal, which fits how much of this ring the pentagon fills. The five identical curled glyphs in the gaps match how the flower sigil is drawn: five small, identical symbols around it act as modifiers that set the type of flower, and possibly how many appear. No directional, inverting or targeting signs are present, so the light simply takes the flower shape around the seal. The Light sigil is small relative to the ring, which suggests a gentle, low-intensity glow.
effect: Creates glowing flowers made of light. The five surrounding modifiers set what kind of flower forms, and the light fades over time.

name: Healingcraft
description: A manga panel showing a glyph drawn on a hanging piece of cloth, with the cloth itself cut off at the edges. The glyph is fully visible. It is a small closed ring crossed by a plus-shaped cross whose four arms extend past the ring to the north, east, south, and west, each ending in a filled dot. There is no element sigil and no other sign.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigil is present, so the glyph sets no element on its own. It matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Selection, a cross drawn through an enclosing shape, though it also resembles Crosshair; reading it as Selection is a guess. Selection is non-directional and confines a spell's effect to the object it is drawn on. Without a sigil the mark works as a modifier or emblem, not as a working seal by itself.
effect: Under the Selection reading, this glyph is a component that would confine a spell's effect to the object or body it marks. It is tied to healingcraft, magic that heals the human body by curing the sick, weak, and injured. The specific spell it would form cannot be determined from the glyph alone.

name: Icy Road
description: An angled view of a seal drawn on stone, with a hand holding a dip pen over its right edge. The left side of the ring and part of the central sigil run off the frame, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be confirmed. The center holds a lattice of straight lines crossing diagonally into a diamond grid, read as the Crystalize sigil. Around it alternate two kinds of signs. Seven Columns signs are visible, each with its bar toward the center and its short stem pointing outward to the ring, sitting at the north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest and northwest. Six unknown signs fill the gaps, each a square containing a small right-angle hook in one corner. The hand covers the eastern part of the seal, and the pen tip rests on the southeast Columns sign, which looks only partly drawn.
justification: The diamond lattice is read as Crystalize, which sets the spell's element: it turns surrounding air or water into crystal or ice. The Columns signs point their stems outward rather than following the usual inward layout, which reads as an inverted arrangement. Inverted Columns spread their effect horizontally instead of beaming it upward, carrying the crystallizing effect past the ring along the ground. The squared hook signs match no known sign. The closest is a Regions sign enclosed in a square, so this is a guess. On that reading, they would mark where the magic manifests relative to the seal, keeping the freezing outside and around the ring rather than inside it. The covered and off-frame parts are assumed to mirror the visible alternating pattern.
effect: Freezes the air into a solid icy surface that extends outward from the seal over a long distance, though only up to a limited range. This assumes the hidden left and covered right portions continue the same symmetric pattern.

name: Illusory Labyrinth
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with a double outer border. The innermost ring is closed, while the outermost line has a small gap at the bottom. The band between the two rings holds eight ornamental knot-and-spiral motifs at the cardinal and intercardinal points. At the center sits an unfamiliar sigil: a dome holding three dots over a horizontal bar, ringed by triangular spikes, with a large solid triangle and bar above it and a fan of streaking bars and lines flowing downward from it. East and west of this sigil are two circles, each enclosing a triangle with a crossbar (like a Strengthening sign) and hooked to the dome by a curved line. Sixteen Columns signs surround the center, all with their crossbars facing outward: four at the north, four at the south, and two each at the upper and lower east and west. Chevron-shaped Regions signs line the inside of the inner ring in four arcs, all pointing counterclockwise around the circle. Three outward-pointing triangles with curled tails sit at the east, west, and south points; these look like inverted Convergence signs. Four branching, antler-like glyphs with trident-shaped forks sit at the intercardinal points.
justification: The central glyph matches none of the five element sigils. Its radiating spikes loosely suggest a fire or light variant, but that is a guess, so the element of the spell cannot be named with confidence. The sixteen Columns signs are spread evenly in every direction, which gives a column-shaped area of effect pushed equally outward with no favored direction. The Regions signs are the key. Instead of pointing inward, outward, or all toward one side, every one of them follows the ring counterclockwise. That sends the magic around the seal and back on itself rather than out of it, which produces a circulating, looping effect. The three tailed triangles are read as inverted Convergence, which is a guess. Inverted, they would spread the magic out rather than focus it to a point, widening the affected area. The circled crossbar triangles are read as Strengthening, also a guess, which would make the result firm and durable. The forked branching glyphs most resemble Glaives, again a guess, and would set how deeply the magic embeds itself. The innermost ring is closed, so the spell is active.
effect: Creates a vast underground labyrinth in which space itself is distorted and loops endlessly. Anyone who walks too far simply reappears where they started, making escape impossible.

name: Light Beacon
description: A manga panel of a hand holding two round objects, each with a seal drawn on it. The rear seal shows a Light sigil at its center, drawn as a square overlapping a rotated square with short lines extending outward. A Columns sign sits at the north point and another at the west point, and part of a third shows at the northeast edge. Small marks at the lower left are too faint to read. The ring is partly visible as an arc on the left, and its lower right portion, including any further signs, is hidden behind the front object and the fingers, so it is not possible to tell whether the ring is open or closed. The front seal, ring closed, has a spiral inside a cloud-like outline at its center, ringed by about eight forked, Columns-like signs.
justification: The Light sigil sets the spell as light magic. Columns signs make magic manifest as a column or beam and control which way it travels. Since the visible Columns signs are spread evenly around the sigil, the beam would be balanced and rise straight up from the seal. This assumes the hidden part of the ring holds matching Columns signs that mirror the visible ones. The central glyph of the front seal matches no known sigil. It is closest to the Wind sigil's spiral, so as a guess it is an air spell, and its forked signs, read as Columns variants, would push that air outward in columns.
effect: Creates a stable beam of light that points straight up from the seal. This assumes the hidden part of the seal mirrors the visible Columns signs.

name: Light-Reducing Spell
description: A round lens with a seal drawn across its glass. The rim forms the ring, which is closed, and the whole seal is fully visible, though the lines are thin and sketchy. A small diamond sits at the center with illegible markings inside it, and faint circles overlap its corners. A larger diamond encloses it. Small triangle signs matching Convergence sit at the corners of the larger diamond and at further points around the ring, roughly eight in total. Short branched lines run between them, with V-shaped strokes near the rim.
justification: No standard element sigil can be matched with certainty. The central diamond is closest to the Diamond sign, which is a guess, and on that reading it limits the spell to what lies within or behind the surface it is drawn on rather than the lens itself. The ring of Convergence signs focuses the magic down to a single point, so the effect would concentrate on the light passing through rather than spreading outward. The branched lines and V-shaped strokes are too faint to name, and they likely further shape where the effect applies.
effect: Blocks out the brightest lights passing through the lens to protect the viewer's eyesight.

name: Lockwax
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a small inner circle holding an unfamiliar sigil shaped like a small circle atop a cross-like stem with upturned arms and split legs. It matches none of the fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigils. Three lines run from the inner circle to the outer ring, dividing the seal into three equal sections. Each section holds the same pair of signs. The first is a long arrow-like sign ending in a triangular head, and the second is a pair of short lines with one bent at a right angle over the other. The three sections repeat with rotational symmetry.
justification: The central glyph matches no known sigil, so its element cannot be named; its separate inner circle sets it apart as the core of the spell. The triangle-tipped arrow most closely resembles Pulling, though this is a guess. Read that way, it draws the target inward toward the seal, which would hold whatever the seal is fixed to shut. The bent pair of short lines most closely resembles Regions, also a guess. Read as Regions, it confines where the magic manifests within each section. Repeating these signs in three equal sections spreads the holding effect evenly around the seal. Together the signs suggest a spell that pulls inward and keeps its target bound in place.
effect: Binds and seals a scroll shut. The level of protection it offers and the way a bound scroll is opened are unknown.

name: Makeover Mask Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a small gap near the top left. There is no element sigil. A Concealment sign fills the center: eight spokes meeting at a point, with an eye at each of the four cardinal ends. A Regions sign sits at the west point and another at the east point, both pointing inward toward the center. At the north point, above the top eye, are three stacked horizontal lines that match no known sign. At the south point, below the bottom eye, is a spiral-shaped glyph that also matches no known sign exactly.
justification: With no sigil, the Concealment sign at the center serves as the core of the seal, so the spell hides the target's original form. Two Regions signs pointing inward keep the magic within the ring rather than projecting it outward, so the effect stays on the surface the seal is drawn on. The three horizontal lines most closely resemble Stability and Level Planes drawn straight. This is a guess, and it would hold the effect steady and level across the surface. The spiral most closely resembles the Purification sign. This is also a guess, and it would add a cleansing quality, so the concealment presents a cleaned-up appearance rather than a different one.
effect: An illusion that conceals the wearer's real face and makes it appear clean and like their best self, essentially working as magic makeup. It is unclear whether the result looks the same for everyone or follows each person's own idea of beauty.

name: Petrification
description: A fully visible seal in black line art, ring closed. The outer edge is a narrow band filled with small Columns-like marks and triple-stroke marks resembling Detection. Four smaller closed circles sit at the cardinal points, each flanked by a pair of small spiral-in-circle signs with corner brackets. The north circle holds faceted diamond shapes and branching snowflake-like strokes with paired Columns signs. The east circle holds water-drop shapes above and below a wavy line. The west circle holds a dotted eye inside a ring of zigzag teeth. The south circle holds curling lines around four small linked circles. At the center is an inner ring lined with a band of tiny marks and dots, enclosing a pinwheel of interlocking squares around a nested square and diamond. On the four cardinal axes between the center and the outer circles sit branching tree-like signs whose arrowheads point inward, framed by scroll curls and ending outward in a three-pronged mark over an arc. At the four intercardinal points sit crossed, hooked glyphs with a stem ending in a small circle, each inside a half-arc. Around these are several Dispersion-like signs, long hooked strokes resembling Envelopment, and short stems tipped with small diamonds resembling Piercing or Sights Set. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The hooked strokes match Envelopment, so the magic wraps around what it targets. The Dispersion-like signs make it pour outward over the surroundings instead of beaming in one direction. The inward-pointing arrowheads on the cardinal axes and the Columns marks in the outer band set where and how far the effect travels. The central pinwheel matches no known sigil. Its nested square and diamond are closest to the Light sigil, but that reading is a guess. It could also be a sub-seal that freezes its target, and that reading fits a petrifying effect better. The four cardinal sub-circles look like nested component seals: water-like in the east, crystal or ice-like in the north, and an eye-like ring in the west. The crossed glyphs at the intercardinal points are closest to Stillness, also a guess, which would hold the effect fixed in place. Read together, the seal spreads an enveloping, immobilizing transformation outward over its whole surroundings, though most individual parts cannot be decoded exactly.
effect: Turns everything nearby, living or inanimate, into an unknown rock-like material, apparently also freezing the petrified targets in time.

name: Rainwarding
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds a large Rain sign drawn inside-out: a curved square with three strokes on each side pointing inward toward an empty middle, the middle stroke of each set longer than the other two. No element sigil is drawn. At the north, south, east, and west points sit four Regions signs, all pointing inward toward the center, each with a straight bar between it and the Rain sign. Between the cardinal points sit eight short diagonal strokes, two near each intercardinal point, each flanked by a single dot on either side.
justification: Rain is semi-directional with radial symmetry, so flipping it inside-out inverts it. Inverted Rain makes an area where the target material cannot exist or is pushed away. The four Regions signs all point inward, which keeps that effect within the ring of the seal. The dotted diagonal strokes match no known sign exactly; the closest is Cooling, which is a line flanked by dots. Reading them as Cooling is a guess, and it would suggest the spell also lowers temperature or damps moisture in the warded area. The straight bars match no known sign; they may be a crossbar that sets the edge of the area, but that is also a guess. With no sigil, the inverted Rain stands in the center as the core of the spell.
effect: Removes water from a given space, creating an area inside the seal's bounds where rain and other water cannot remain and are pushed out.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a wind sigil at the center flanked by three short strokes on each side. Six inward-pointing Levitation signs sit at the east and west points and at four positions near the top and bottom, each with its crossbar toward the ring. Just outside each Levitation sign is an unidentified sign of two short parallel straight lines, like an equal sign, for six in total. At the north and south points and at four positions on the left and right sides sit six long Columns signs, each with its crossbar against the ring and joined near the center by a Regions chevron pointing inward. The Columns and Regions pairs and the Levitation signs alternate around the ring in a radially symmetric layout.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves air, and its modest size relative to the ring points to a steady rather than violent output. All six Columns signs are balanced, so they give the magic a column-shaped area of effect without favoring any side, and their length adds pressure to the flow. The inward-pointing Regions chevrons confine the magic to the space within the ring, so the air is driven straight out from the seal's face. The six balanced, inward-pointing Levitation signs reinforce that lift and propulsion, and their length sets how hard the air pushes. The equal-sign glyph matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Stability and Level Planes, and reading it that way is a guess. On that reading, it would keep the air stream level and stable as it flows.
effect: Creates a steady gust of wind from the face of the seal that pushes against a sail to propel a water vehicle. The spell runs only while the ring is closed. Leaving a small gap in the ring switches it off, and pressing the gap shut turns it back on.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: A round disc carrying a seal, with its right edge cut off by the frame and its top covered by a block. A small wind sigil sits at the center. Around it, at the west, southwest, northwest and south, are groups of three marks that read outward to inward: two short parallel lines like an equal sign, then a Columns sign with its crossbar toward the rim, then an arrowhead pointing inward. Together the Columns and arrowhead look much like a Levitation sign. Smaller lone arrows, which read as Levitation signs, point inward between these groups. The block at the top bears one more Columns-and-arrow mark pointing down toward the center. The east side is partly visible, showing only the tips of matching arrows. No separate drawn ring line is visible, so whether the ring is open or closed cannot be read.
justification: The wind sigil makes this a spell that moves existing air. Its small size relative to the seal suggests a moderate, steady output rather than a violent blast. The Columns signs give the magic a column-shaped area and push it in a direction. The arrowheads read as Regions signs, and with the lone Levitation signs they all point inward, so the air movement is gathered over the seal rather than scattered outside it. The equal-sign marks match no known sign exactly. The closest is Stability and Level Planes, which is a guess; on that reading they keep the airflow steady and level. I assume the hidden right side mirrors the visible left, since the layout is radially repeated.
effect: Produces a steady, continuous gust of wind that pushes a sail, propelling a water vessel forward. This assumes the hidden right side mirrors the visible left.

name: River Ferry Seal
description: A large round disk with a seal drawn on it. A standing figure covers the left half, so roughly half the seal is partly visible and the ring cannot be confirmed as open or closed. A wind sigil sits at the center, with its spiral partly hidden behind the figure's arm and its short side ticks visible to its right. Close around the sigil, three Levitation signs are visible at the north-east, east and south-east, arrows pointing inward. Farther out are three large glyphs, each looking like a Columns sign joined with an inward-pointing Regions sign, at the north-east, east and south-east. Another sits at the top edge inside a squared frame, and a cut-off one sits at the bottom. About four small marks shaped like an equal sign, two short parallel lines, sit between these outer glyphs.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element, so the spell moves air rather than creating it. The inward-pointing Levitation signs and the Columns-with-Regions glyphs are directional signs, and they drive the air out in a column. Because the visible half appears evenly spaced, I assume the hidden half mirrors it and the signs are balanced. The equal-sign marks match no known sign exactly. The closest is Stability and Level Planes, which is a guess. On that reading they keep the push steady and level instead of erratic.
