effect: Assuming the hidden half mirrors the visible half, the spell produces a steady, level gust of wind that pushes against a sail to propel a water vehicle forward.

name: Scalewolf Curse
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with a double ring, both rings closed. Sixteen solid triangles point outward from the outer ring: four large ones at the north, south, east and west points, with three smaller ones evenly spaced between each pair. At the center are three dots arranged in a triangle, one above and two below, forming the sigil. A wide arch curves over the dots and meets a horizontal bar beneath them. Four vertical stems hang from this bar, each ending in an open fork shaped like an inverted V.
justification: The three-dot sigil sets the kind of magic, but it matches none of the elemental sigils. The arch over the bar resembles a Stretch sign closed off by a line. Read that way, it would reshape whatever lies under it into a new form, though this is a guess. Each forked stem is closest to a Launch sign on a stalk, also a guess. Four of them would drive the change outward from the seal in strong bursts. The outward-pointing triangles on the outer ring are closest to inverted Convergence, another guess. They would spread the magic over the whole target rather than focusing it on one point. Because they are attached outside the ring like Glaives, they may also set how deeply the magic embeds into flesh. Together, these signs suggest a spell that forces a deep, body-wide change of form.
effect: A forbidden spell that permanently transforms a person's body. It fuses the target with creature material they are wearing, such as scalewolf fur and scales, and turns them into that creature.

name: Sealchair Spell
description: A manga panel showing a large seal drawn on a wooden surface between two thick wooden legs, rendered in halftone. A main oval ring, ring closed, holds a dense cross-hatched central glyph surrounded by many tiny signs. Inside the ring sit three clusters of small linked loops, at the upper left, lower left, and lower right. Around the main ring are satellite seals joined to it by short lines: several large circles at the left, upper right, right, and lower left, plus a series of small circles along the edges. The satellites at the frame edges are partly visible, and most signs in the main ring and the satellites are too small and too blurred by the screentone to identify.
justification: The central glyph matches no known element sigil at this resolution, so the kind of magic cannot be read directly. The looped clusters most closely resemble the Dancing Puppets sign, though this is a guess. If that reading is right, they would allow deliberate, controlled movement of the object the seal is drawn on. The many satellite seals joined to the main ring suggest separate sub-spells feeding into one larger working, but their contents cannot be decoded because they are too small or cut off at the frame edges.
effect: The effect cannot be fully determined from the readable glyphs. The spell is known to control the movement of a legged chair, letting it walk and carry a seated person. The Dancing Puppets-like loops are consistent with that kind of guided movement.

name: Slime Rendering Seal
description: A manga panel of a body outline lying flat with a network of seal lines drawn across it. A large white speech bubble covers the abdomen, hips and upper thighs. On the chest is a small ring, ring closed, with a curled spiral glyph at its center. About six lines run out from this ring, each ending in a three-pronged fork that matches Glaives. Two small signs made of a circle joined to a line, resembling Solidification, sit on the torso beside the ring. A line with herringbone branches runs from the chest ring down to a second ring on the belly. That ring holds a curled glyph and is partly visible, with much of it hidden behind the speech bubble. Lines run down both arms and the visible leg, crossed by bands at the elbows, wrists, knees and ankles, and end in more Glaives-like forks. The legs also carry herringbone marks. The rest of the seal network is hidden by the bubble.
justification: The forked endings are Glaives. They set how deeply the magic embeds itself into flesh, and they are allowed to extend outside the ring as long as they stay connected to it. Their spread over the chest and limbs means the magic is driven through the whole body. The chest spiral matches no sign exactly. It is closest to the asymmetric Wind sign or the Purification sign, though this is a guess. Read as Purification, it would separate and break down the body's matter. The circle-and-line marks read as Solidification, which normally makes magic more solid, so here they likely give the transformed matter a cohesive, gelatinous consistency; this is also a guess. The herringbone lines match no known sign. The belly ring cannot be decoded because the speech bubble covers it.
effect: Transforms the target into slime. The Glaives drive the effect deep into the flesh of the whole body.

name: Smokesculpting Seal
description: A fully visible seal drawn on a plain background, ring closed. At the center is a tight spiral with a vertical line running through it. Above the spiral, the line ends at the north point in a starburst. Below it, the line ends in two stacked chevrons pointing down, like the arrowhead of a Pulling sign. Two zigzag signs that match Crushing sit to the left and right of the spiral, both inverted. Four Columns signs surround it: two upright above and two inverted below. Four teardrop signs, shaped like the droplets of the water sigil, sit at the intercardinal points. At the east and west points are two starburst signs crossed with a short line, like an asterisk fused with a Columns sign.
justification: The central spiral matches no known sigil or sign. The closest match is the curl of the Wind sign or the spiral of the wind sigil, so reading it as an air or wind glyph is a guess. On that reading it gives the spell an airborne medium such as smoke. The droplet signs are also a guess: as pieces of the water sigil they could add a vapor or steam quality. Inverted Crushing signs reform crushed or broken material back into its original shape. The Columns signs and the downward chevrons send the effect up from the seal in a column, and the starbursts at north, east and west may spread that column outward. Together, these suggest a spell that rebuilds the shape of something in rising smoke rather than in the material itself.
effect: Creates a smoke, or possibly steam, sculpture that recreates the original shape of nearby ingredients, such as those added to tea. Like a reforming spell, it rebuilds the ingredients' form, but out of smoke instead of the ingredients themselves.

name: Smokesculpting Seal
description: Two manga panels. The upper panel has a fully visible diagram of a seal with the ring closed. At the center is a spiral crossed by a vertical line. The line runs north to an asterisk-like sign and south to a downward-pointing arrow with stacked chevrons. Beside the spiral to the east and west sit two Crushing signs turned sideways, apparently inverted. Four Columns signs sit at the diagonals around the center, the upper pair upright and the lower pair flipped. Four teardrop shapes like the drops of the water sigil sit at the outer diagonals. At the east and west edges are two signs that look like an asterisk fused with a Columns stem pointing inward. The lower panel shows the same seal drawn small on a saucer, fully visible but too small to read in detail, with a thumb at the saucer's edge.
justification: The central spiral matches no known sigil. Its curl is closest to the spiral of the wind sigil, so reading it as a wind-family or smoke glyph is a guess that fits a spell made of airborne vapor. The inverted Crushing signs reverse crushing, so material that has broken apart takes back its original shape. The Columns signs send the effect upward in a column above the seal. The teardrop signs are a guess at water drops, which would add moisture or steam to the vapor. The asterisk-and-stem signs and the arrow through the center are unknown; they may be Columns or Pulling variants that draw material in and lift it. Together these suggest a spell that rebuilds the shape of material as rising vapor.
effect: Creates a sculpture of smoke, or possibly steam, that recreates the original shape of nearby ingredients. Like reverse crushing, it reforms the ingredients' shapes, but it builds them out of smoke rather than restoring the ingredients themselves.

name: Snowfending
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a large fire sigil at the center. A Stillness sign sits at the east point and another at the west point. At the north and south points sit S-shaped curl signs, mirrored top to bottom, that resemble the central stroke of the wind sigil without its dashes. Four Stability and Level Planes signs flank them, two beside the north curl and two beside the south curl. At the four intercardinal points sit four forked, Y-like signs, each a stem with two branching strokes, that match no known sign exactly.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as fire, here heat, and its large size relative to the ring means a strong effect. Stillness holds a magical effect static in one location, so the heat stays fixed over the area instead of moving or dissipating. Stability and Level Planes keep the effect balanced in a level plane, which spreads the held heat as a steady layer above the seal. The north and south curls most closely resemble the wind sigil's stroke, so as a guess they add an air-moving element that carries the warmth. The forked intercardinal signs are closest to Gathering, also a guess, which would let the spell draw on surrounding material or air to sustain the effect.
effect: Holds a steady layer of heat in place over an area so that falling snow melts and is kept off whatever lies beneath it through the winter.

name: Snugstone Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background. The ring is open, with a gap at the lower left. A fire sigil sits at the center, fairly small relative to the ring. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points (northeast, northwest, southeast, southwest), each drawn with its crossbar toward the center and its stem toward the ring. At each of the four cardinal points (north, east, south, west) sits an identical glyph made of a large U-shaped arc with a smaller U-shaped arc nested inside, both opening outward toward the ring.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a fire spell, and its modest size keeps the output low. The Columns signs face the reverse of their usual direction, so they read as inverted Columns. Inverted Columns spreads its effect horizontally and outward, much like Dispersion, rather than as a vertical beam. The nested double arcs match no known sign exactly. The closest is Binding, which is also two stacked arcs, so this reading is a guess. As Binding, they would hold the fire's energy together and keep it from moving off as flame. Together, a small fire sigil, outward-spreading inverted Columns, and a holding modifier produce gentle heat radiating in all directions with no flame. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate as drawn.
effect: Radiates gentle warmth outward without producing a flame. The heat is balanced to the size of the seal so that it feels warm to the touch but is never hot enough to burn.

name: Snugstone Spell
description: A manga panel of a round, cracked stone with a seal drawn on it. The seal is fully visible but low in detail. Several dark cracks run across it from the left edge through the center, cutting through the sigil and some signs. The ring follows the rim of the stone and is crossed by these cracks, so whether it is open or closed cannot be confirmed. A fire sigil sits at the center, partly broken up by the cracks. A Columns sign sits at the south point, drawn inverted with its crossbar toward the center. A similar inverted Columns-like sign appears at the east point. Curled, hook-shaped signs sit at the northwest, northeast, southwest and southeast points. The west point is mostly hidden by the cracks near the rim.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as fire or heat. Inverted Columns spread their effect horizontally instead of sending it up as a beam, much like Dispersion, so the heat leaks outward around the stone rather than shooting off in one direction. The curled signs match no known sign exactly. Their closest match is the Purification sign's curl, but that is a guess. On that reading they would refine or temper the fire, which fits a spell that gives off gentle heat without producing a flame. The sigil looks modest in size relative to the ring, which keeps the intensity low.
effect: Radiates steady warmth outward from the stone without producing a flame. It is balanced to the size of the seal so the stone stays warm to the touch but never hot enough to burn.

name: Tracking Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with its outer ring closed. There is no element sigil. A long horizontal line crosses the whole ring through the center, overlaid by a zigzag of four peaks that runs edge to edge. Inside the ring are two partial inner arcs. One runs from the top around the left side and ends in a small forked hook. The other runs from the bottom around the right side and ends in a matching hook. At the north a vertical stem hangs from the inner arc down to a small circle, and at the south the same glyph appears flipped. In the northeast and southwest sits a diamond crossed by two curved lines. In the northwest and southeast sits a vertical stroke crossed by several short horizontal bars with diagonal ticks. The whole layout has point symmetry: each glyph in one half is rotated 180 degrees in the other.
justification: None of these glyphs exactly matches a known sign, so each reading is a guess. The diamond glyphs are closest to Diamond, which limits the spell to objects near the seal rather than the item it is drawn on. Their crossing curves resemble Coil, though they are more likely part of the same glyph. The barred glyphs are closest to Concealment, which would keep the effect hidden. The hooked inner arcs resemble Envelopment, which wraps an effect around a target. The stem-and-circle glyphs are closest to one half of Solidification, which would make the effect hold firm. The central zigzag is closest to a stretched Crushing sign laid along a line, but here it more likely acts as a dividing or linking line between the two mirrored halves. Read together without a sigil, these suggest a hidden effect that wraps around and stays fixed to a nearby target object, which fits marking an item so it can be followed.
effect: Marks a magical item and lets it be tracked. How each individual glyph contributes to this is unknown.

name: Twinned Bottles
description: A fully visible round medallion with a seal, ring closed. No element sigil is present. At the center is an hourglass figure of two triangles meeting at a point, resembling a Reflection sign, with an extra curved stroke crossing through it diagonally. Four corner brackets frame this figure, one at each corner with the angle pointing outward, arranged like a single-line Expansion sign. A short horizontal dash sits at the east point and another at the west point. Around the inner edge of the ring is a band of about ten identical small glyphs, evenly spaced. Each is a pair of curved brackets enclosing short strokes. These glyphs match no known sign exactly.
justification: With no element sigil, the seal is built entirely from signs. The central figure is closest to Reflection, which targets a mirrored counterpart. Here that is read as a guess to mean this seal acts on a matching twin seal. The outward-pointing corners are closest to Expansion, a semi-directional sign that sets the size or amount of what the spell affects, so they likely balance quantity. The repeated perimeter glyphs most resemble Holding, which keeps contents in a defined shape. That is also a guess, read here as holding the contents within the vessel. The east and west dashes may be paired directional marks linking the two sides. Taken together, a mirrored link plus amount control plus holding gives a spell that keeps two vessels' contents in balance.
effect: Keeps the contents of two separate vessels evenly split, no matter how far apart they are. It activates as liquid runs along the shallow etched lines of the seal.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with no sigil. Eight Columns signs are spaced evenly just inside the ring at the north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, and northwest points. All eight share one orientation, with the crossbar toward the ring and the stem pointing toward the center. Around the empty center sit four closed half-disc glyphs in a pinwheel: the north one curves west, the east one curves north, the south one curves east, and the west one curves south. Four small X-shaped glyphs sit at the intercardinal points between the half-discs.
justification: The seal has no sigil, so no element is set. The eight Columns signs are balanced on all sides, which by the Columns rule sends the magic straight up as a column above the seal rather than to one side. The X glyphs match no known sign exactly. As a guess, they are read as Collection, an X closed on one side, which would draw in material from above and around the seal. The half-discs also match no known sign. As a guess, they are read as Binding-like arcs that bind material into one unit. Their rotational pinwheel layout suggests a twisting motion, much as angled Pulling signs twist.
effect: The spell's effect is not known. A tentative reading from its signs is that it gathers nearby material, binds it, and lifts it straight up from the seal as a column, possibly with a twisting motion. Because there is no sigil, the kind of material it acts on cannot be determined from the image.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with a hand-drawn, wavy ring that is closed. At the center is an irregular glyph made of a plus-shaped cross with two long, crossing petal loops laid over it in an X. No standard element sigil is present. Eight Columns signs are evenly spaced around the center at the four cardinal and four intercardinal points. All eight face the same way, with the crossbar toward the center and the stem pointing out toward the ring.
justification: The central glyph matches no known sigil or sign. The closest match is Billow, whose looped petals it resembles, though here only two loops cross over a cross. This reading is a guess. Billow is a sign that can take the place of a sigil at the center and turns material into a soft, cloud-like mass. The eight Columns signs are evenly balanced, so no direction has more signs than another. They therefore push the effect straight up from the seal as a column rather than off to one side. With no Collection or Gathering sign, nothing in the seal draws in outside material, so the effect would act on whatever is already over the seal.
effect: If the central glyph is read as a variant of Billow, the spell turns material above the seal into a fluffy, cloud-like mass and raises it straight up in a column. This reading of the central glyph is a guess, so the exact effect is uncertain.

name: Unknown Magic
description: Five separate rings drawn apart from one another, all fully visible. At the top is a small closed ring holding a plain plus-shaped cross. To the upper right is a closed ring holding a small upright triangle with one point facing north. In the middle is the largest ring, closed, holding a single spiral that winds about three times from the center outward. At the lower left is a ring left open at its lower right, with two long curved strokes crossing each other and running past the ring on both sides. At the lower right is a ring open at the bottom, holding one diagonal line crossed by three short parallel strokes. None of the five glyphs exactly matches a known sigil or sign.
justification: Every reading here is a guess. The central spiral is closest to the coil of the wind sigil, or to its whorling variant, so that ring most likely holds a wind-type sigil that moves air in a rotating pattern, and its closed ring would let it activate. The plus is closest to Crosshair, which lacks the central gap here, so it is read as a targeting sign on its own with no sigil to act on. The upright triangle is closest to Convergence, though Convergence is drawn point-down. Read that way, this one points north rather than toward a center, which could mean inverted Convergence that spreads magic out instead of focusing it. The two crossing curves are closest to Coil, which softens physical matter. The line with three crossbars is closest to Detection, read only loosely from its three parallel strokes. The lower-left and lower-right rings are both open, so those two would not activate as drawn. Since each ring stands alone, the five do not combine into a single seal.
effect: The purpose of these seals is not established. On the guessed readings, the closed spiral ring would stir air in a whirling motion. The plus and the triangle rings would act only as targeting and focusing or spreading components. The two open rings, read as softening and sensing, would stay inert until their rings are closed.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a single composite glyph: a tall arch with two long legs running downward, crossed at mid-height by a horizontal line that ends in a small open circle on each side. No element sigil for fire, water, earth, wind, or light is present. Six Columns signs surround the center at even intervals (north, south, and the four points between them at roughly sixty degrees), each turned sideways so its stem runs along the ring rather than toward the center. All six stems point clockwise. Six small open circles alternate with the Columns signs around the ring.
justification: There is no element sigil, so the seal does not name its own material. The horizontal bar with a circle on each end most closely resembles a Solidification sign laid on its side, and the arch over it loosely resembles a Stretch sign with lengthened legs. Both readings are guesses. Taken together, they suggest that whatever the seal acts on is made firmer and held in a shaped form. Columns is directional, and changing its angle changes the direction in which the magic manifests. With all six turned the same way along the ring, the push is tangential rather than outward, which suggests a clockwise circling motion. The six small circles match no known sign; their closest match is the end circles of Solidification, but this is a guess and their role cannot be stated with confidence.
effect: The exact effect of this seal is unknown. Based on the guessed reading of its signs, it likely firms up and holds its target in a shaped form while driving it around the seal in a clockwise circle. Because it has no element sigil, what material it acts on cannot be determined.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, bounded by several concentric rings. Between the two innermost rings runs a band of small repeated tick and hook marks circling the whole seal. At the center is a triangle sigil, close to the fire sigil, with a small circle on each of its three corners or edges. A short line extends outward from each circle, three spokes in all. Around the center sit eight identical units at the cardinal and intercardinal points. Reading outward from the center, each unit has a dot, then a Columns-like sign with its crossbar toward the rim, flanked by two parallel strokes, then a long zigzag with three peaks near the rim. Between each pair of units is a long S-shaped wavy stroke, eight in all, running from near the center toward the rim.
justification: The triangle sets the element as fire, so this is a fire-type spell. The circles and spokes on the triangle mark a variant of the fire sigil that matches no known sigil. The sigil is small relative to the ring, which points to moderate intensity. Eight Columns signs balanced all the way around send the magic out in columns in every direction equally rather than toward one side. The two parallel strokes beside each Columns are a guess, read as reinforcing that output. The three-peak zigzags most closely match an elongated Crushing sign, also a guess. Crushing is semi-directional, so a larger sign gives a stronger effect, and an inverted one reforms material instead of breaking it apart. The S-shaped strokes most closely resemble a single-stroke Stability and Level Planes or the Wind sign, which is a guess. Under the first reading they would keep the effect level and balanced. The band of repeated marks between the inner rings resembles Windows, which lines a seal like an extra ring, but this match is uncertain.
effect: The spell is not identified by name, so its effect is a tentative reading of the glyphs. It most likely produces fire that radiates outward in eight balanced columns around the seal. The Crushing-like signs would break apart, or if inverted reform, what the flames reach. The wavy strokes would keep the effect level and stable.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a water sigil at the center. The sigil is small relative to the ring. Eight identical Levitation signs surround it, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point (north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest). Each has its base bar toward the ring and its arrowhead pointing inward toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The water sigil sets the element: manipulating, collecting, or creating water. Levitation floats a target into the air. When its signs are balanced, it tends to shape the target into a sphere. Here all eight point inward in an evenly spaced, symmetrical arrangement, so the lift is balanced with no net direction. The modest sigil size suggests a gentle, low-intensity effect.
effect: Likely lifts water into the air above the seal and holds it there as a floating sphere, with the balanced Levitation signs keeping it centered rather than sending it in any direction.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a light sigil at the center: a square with a smaller diamond inside and a short line extending from each side. Eight Dispersion signs surround it, one at each cardinal and intercardinal point (north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest). All eight are oriented the same way, with the stem pointing outward toward the ring and the curved arc facing the sigil. The sigil is small relative to the ring.
justification: The light sigil sets the element as light, a fire-domain magic that creates and manipulates light that fades over time. Dispersion makes a seal's magic pour outward rather than beam in one direction. Because the eight Dispersion signs are equal in size and evenly spaced, no direction is favored, so the light should spread evenly all around the seal. The small sigil points to a modest intensity. The precise behavior of this seal is not established, so this reading rests on the known sign rules alone.
effect: Likely produces a gentle glow that spreads evenly outward in all directions from the seal, like a soft lamp, and slowly fades over time. The exact function of this seal is not known.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A fire sigil sits at the center, small relative to the ring. Eight Columns signs are evenly spaced around it at the north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, and northwest points. All eight share the same orientation, with the crossbar toward the ring and the stem pointing in toward the sigil. No other signs are present.
justification: The fire sigil makes this a spell that creates or controls flame or heat, and its modest size relative to the ring points to moderate intensity. Columns gives the magic a column-shaped area of effect, and more Columns signs widen its range or the amount of magic produced. Because all eight are identical and spaced evenly, the signs are balanced with no favored side, so the column is not pushed toward any direction and should rise straight up from the seal.
effect: Produces a steady column of fire rising straight up from the seal, at moderate strength and spread evenly across the seal's area.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a triangle whose three corners loop over into rounded petals, with a small hollow circle just beyond each corner. Between the corners, on each of the three sides of the triangle, sits a cluster of three short rays pointing outward, much like the Aeriforms Defined sign. Around this, arranged in a pinwheel with threefold rotational symmetry, are six angle-shaped signs with one long and one short arm, resembling Regions chevrons. There are also six groups of three parallel strokes of increasing length, resembling Detection, and three single short diagonal strokes. All of these outer marks are tilted the same way around the ring rather than pointing straight inward or outward.
justification: The central glyph matches no known sigil exactly. Its closest match is the Fire sigil, since both are a triangle with outward rays, so the element is read as fire as a guess; the three-ray clusters could instead mark a wind or air variant, as they copy the Aeriforms Defined design. The angled chevrons are read as Regions, also a guess, and Regions decides where magic manifests relative to the seal. Because every chevron is turned the same way around the ring, the magic would be driven sideways around the circle rather than inward or outward, which suggests a rotating, swirling manifestation. The graduated triple strokes are closest to Detection, again a guess, and Detection's function is unclear. The single strokes match no known sign.
effect: The exact effect is unknown. Read through the closest known signs, it most likely produces fire or heat, or possibly moving air, that swirls in a rotating pattern around the seal.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with no element sigil. A Billow sign sits at the center in place of a sigil. Around it, four Collection signs sit at the north, east, south, and west points, each with its closed triangle facing outward and its open, splayed side facing the center. Farther out at the same four cardinal points are four Levitation signs, each with its base bar toward the ring and its arrow pointing inward. At the four intercardinal points sit four matching unfamiliar glyphs, each a long diagonal stroke crossed by three perpendicular strokes: short, long, short.
justification: Billow takes the place of a sigil and turns available material into a soft, fluffy cloud. The four inward-facing Collection signs gather material from above and around the seal for the spell to use, which supplies Billow with something to convert. Four balanced Levitation signs pointing inward float the result above the seal, and balanced Levitation tends to hold it in a rounded mass. The intercardinal glyph matches no known sign. Its closest match is Crosshair, which is also built from crossing strokes, but this reading is a guess. Read that way, the four glyphs would aim the effect at whatever lies at their shorter ends.
effect: Gathers loose material from around the seal and turns it into a fluffy, comfortable cloud that floats above the seal. If the intercardinal glyphs act like Crosshair, they would also direct the cloud toward a chosen target.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, with the ring closed. A large sigil fills the center. It resembles the earth sigil, with a top bar, a vertical stem and a V-shaped base meeting at the bottom of the stem. It differs in two ways: small open circles replace the two dots, and a second horizontal bar sits below the point of the V. At the north and south sit long horizontal bars, each carrying two half-circle bumps. The north bumps face up and the south bumps face down, so both pairs face outward toward the ring. At the east and west sit pairs of nested arcs, a large outer arc and a smaller inner one, with their convex sides toward the center. Each pair has a small open circle beside it on the rim side. The whole seal is mirror-symmetric left to right and top to bottom.
justification: The central glyph reads as a variant of the earth sigil, so this is earth magic acting on solid material such as stone, sand or soil. Its large size relative to the ring points to a strong effect. The nested arcs at east and west most closely match the Binding sign, which halts the movement of material and holds it together as a single unit; the added circles make this a guess. The barred signs at north and south match no known sign. Their closest match is Partition, also a guess, which outlines the borders of an area of effect; the outward-facing bumps would push those borders toward the ring. On that reading, the seal gathers earth inside a bounded area and binds it into one solid mass.
effect: The effect of this seal is not established. Read from its signs, it is likely an earth spell that binds solid material into a single unit inside a defined boundary. This reading rests on guessed matches for the Binding-like and Partition-like signs.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A large earth sigil fills the center: a long horizontal bar with a vertical stem dropping to the point of a wide V, with one dot at the east and one at the west. Its V arms are straight and lack the small hooks of the usual earth sigil. Above it, at the north, sits a single large V-shaped sign that looks like a Regions sign with its point aimed inward at the center. Below it, at the south, is a single long horizontal bar that matches no known sign.
justification: The earth sigil sets the element, so the spell works on solid matter such as stone, sand, soil or wood. Its size relative to the ring is large, which points to a strong effect. The northern glyph is read as one Regions sign pointing toward the center and toward the south side. When all Regions signs in a seal point the same way, the magic is sent that way, so this lone sign would drive the earth magic south. The southern bar matches no known sign. As a guess, its closest match is the Projection sign without its two short legs, which would push the effect outward past that edge of the ring.
effect: The exact effect of this seal is unknown. Read through its signs, it would strongly move or shape solid earth material and push it in one direction, toward the side marked by the bar.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A large S-shaped curve runs across the center from lower left to upper right, each end curling inward into a small loop, with a small half-circle bump on the outer edge of each lobe. Two long arrow signs sit inside the lobes: on the west side an arrow points north, and on the east side a matching arrow points south. The arrows have open chevron heads and no crossbar at the base. The whole design has two-fold rotational symmetry, with no other signs.
justification: The central S-curve matches no known sigil exactly. The closest match is the Wind sigil's spiral S, read here as a wind-family sigil, and its curled, rotating form is also close to Whorling Wind; both readings are guesses. The arrows are closest to Levitation without its base bar, or to a Regions chevron on a long shaft; this is also a guess. Read as directional signs, two equal arrows pointing in opposite directions on opposite sides of the center do not cancel into a single push. Like an angled Pulling sign, which adds a twist, the offset, opposed pair would turn the magic around the center. Under this reading, the wind-type sigil sets the element and the paired arrows set a rotating motion.
effect: The effect cannot be confirmed from known sign definitions. As a tentative reading, the seal moves air in opposite directions on either side of its center, turning it into a rotating or swirling current over the seal.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with the ring closed. At the center is a small empty circle with no element sigil inside it. Four Columns signs radiate from this inner circle to the north, east, south, and west, forming an even cross. Each sign has a very long stem that touches the inner circle and a crossbar near the outer ring. All four are equal in length, and nothing else is drawn inside the seal.
justification: There is no element sigil, so nothing sets what kind of magic the seal produces. The inner circle is the closest thing to a central glyph. It matches no known sign exactly; reading it as an inner ring that links the four signs, similar to how Solidification joins circles with straight lines, is a guess. Columns gives an area of effect shaped like a column and pushes magic in a set direction, and a longer sign adds more pressure or power. Here four equally elongated Columns signs are balanced at the cardinal points, so no single direction dominates. Their long stems all run into the central circle, so the reading is that strong, evenly balanced column pressure is focused on the center.
effect: The exact effect of this seal is unknown. Read from its signs, it would exert strong, even column-shaped pressure from all four sides toward a central point. With no sigil, it has no set element and works on whatever the inner circle defines; this reading is a guess.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds a Selection sign: a square crossed by a vertical and a horizontal line that both extend well beyond its edges. There is no element sigil. Four Columns signs sit at the northeast, northwest, southeast, and southwest points. All four share the same orientation, with the crossbar facing the center and the stem reaching toward the ring. The arrangement is fully symmetric.
justification: With no element sigil, the seal has no fire, water, earth, wind, or light magic to produce. Its behavior comes entirely from its signs. Selection limits a spell to the object the seal is drawn on. Columns creates a column-shaped area of effect and controls the direction an object proceeds. The four Columns signs are equal in number and length on every side, so no direction is favored, and the force should act straight up from the seal rather than off to one side. Read together, the seal applies Columns force only to the object bearing it. This combined reading is an interpretation, since the full spell has no established description.
effect: The exact effect is not established. Reading the signs, it most likely pushes or raises the object the seal is drawn on straight up along a column, without affecting anything around it.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with no recognizable element sigil. At the center, two diagonal lines cross in an X, and four triangles sit between its arms, all pointing inward. The north and south triangles each carry a stem running outward, like two Pulling signs facing each other. The east and west triangles have no stems and resemble Convergence signs. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, each with its crossbar toward the ring and its stem pointing inward. A Convergence sign at north and another at south both point toward the center. At west and east sit a mirrored pair of unknown glyphs: a circle split by a vertical line, a horizontal line running from the circle's center outward past its edge, and a downward-pointing triangle resting on top.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigil is present, so the element cannot be read. The central cluster matches no known sigil or sign. My best guess is that it combines Pulling and Convergence, drawing magic inward and focusing it at one point. The four Columns signs are balanced, so they push their effect evenly rather than favoring one direction. The two inward Convergence signs reinforce the focusing. The east and west glyphs most resemble an Orb sign, a circle crossed by a line, fused with a Convergence triangle. This reading is a guess, but it suggests the focused material collects in a spherical space. Taken together, the seal appears to pull material in, compact it, and hold it in a balanced sphere at the center.
effect: The exact effect of this seal is not known. A tentative reading of its signs suggests it draws material inward and packs it into a dense sphere centered above the seal. With no element sigil present, what kind of material or magic it acts on cannot be determined.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center sits a large upward-pointing triangle with three short rays at each of three spots: upper left, upper right, and below. It looks like a fire sigil whose single strokes have been tripled. Three Convergence signs surround it. One sits at north with its point toward the center, and one each sits at the lower left and lower right with their points facing down. Eight Columns signs form an inner ring, each with its crossbar toward the center and its stem pointing outward. Near the edge, four Dispersion signs mark the north, east, south, and west points, each with its curve facing the center. Between them, sixteen more Columns signs, four per quadrant, face the same way as the inner ones. The layout is radially symmetric.
justification: The center glyph matches no reference sigil exactly. Its closest match is the Fire sigil, and reading it as a fire variant with stronger flare marks is a guess. On that reading the spell creates or controls flame, and the sigil is moderately sized against the ring, giving solid intensity. Twenty-four Columns signs all point the same way and are balanced around the ring. Columns make the magic manifest as a column, and a high count widens its range and the amount of magic produced, so the result is a broad upward pillar rather than a beam aimed to one side. The four Dispersion signs make part of that magic pour outward instead of beaming straight up. The three Convergence signs pull the magic toward a single point and pack it tighter, keeping the column focused at its core.
effect: This seal is not otherwise identified, so its effect is read only from its signs. Taking the center glyph as a fire variant, it likely raises a large, concentrated pillar of flame above the seal, with some fire spilling outward around its base.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A water sigil, an S-curve flanked by two drops, sits at the center. Directly above it is a triangular cluster of three small hollow circles, and an inverted matching cluster of three sits directly below it. Sixteen signs alternate evenly around the ring. Eight are T-shaped Columns signs with the crossbar toward the rim and the stem toward the center. The other eight are Pulling signs, each an arrow with a small triangle on the shaft and a large arrowhead pointing inward at the sigil.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its moderate size suggests moderate intensity. The eight Pulling signs all point inward, so the magic draws water toward the seal. They lie radially rather than angled, so there is no twisting. The eight evenly spaced Columns signs are balanced, which points the column straight up out of the seal rather than to one side. The small hollow circle clusters match no known sign. Their closest match is the circles of Solidification, so as a guess they firm up the gathered water into a more solid, held form.
effect: Draws surrounding water inward toward the seal and sends it up from the seal in a column, likely holding it in a firmer, more cohesive mass. This reading assumes the circle clusters act like Solidification.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. At the center is a light sigil: a square with a diamond inside it, a dot at the very center, and four lines running out from the diamond's points to the north, east, south and west. A short diagonal line runs out from each of the square's four corners and ends in a crossbar, like a Columns sign joined to the sigil. Around the sigil is a ring of eight T-shaped Columns signs, evenly spaced and each tilted slightly clockwise, with the crossbar facing the ring and the stem pointing toward the center. In the outer band, alternating with the Columns, are eight identical glyphs made of two interlocking open square brackets. Where the brackets overlap they form a small closed square. These are also turned the same way, giving the seal a pinwheel layout.
justification: The light sigil sets the element, so the spell makes and shapes light. Its size is moderate relative to the ring, which suggests moderate intensity. Eight balanced Columns signs, plus the four joined to the sigil's corners, send that light out in columns, and their even count keeps it from favouring any one direction. The interlocking bracket glyph matches no known sign. Its closest match is Expansion, whose corner brackets it resembles, but that reading is a guess. Read as Expansion with corners pointing outward, it would make the manifested light grow in size. The shared clockwise tilt of every outer sign suggests the effect may also turn or spread in a rotating way.
effect: Likely creates light and sends it out in columns of moderate strength, balanced on all sides, with the light enlarging as it spreads and possibly turning in a pinwheel motion. This reading assumes the unknown bracket glyphs act like Expansion.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A fire sigil sits at the center at moderate size. It is drawn as a variant: the two side ticks cross the upper sides of the triangle, and the stem passes through the base and extends above and below it. A single dot marks the north point. Below it is a large M-shaped zigzag whose legs splay outward at the base, with two Columns-like branches attached to each leg, their crossbars facing outward. A Regions sign sits at the northwest and another at the northeast, each with its point aimed toward the center. At the west and east are a mirrored pair of curling S-shaped glyphs, each with a dot inside its lower loop; these most resemble the Sign of Wind or the spiral of the wind sigil. At the southwest and southeast are Columns signs with doubled crossbars near the ring and stems pointing inward, each with a Regions sign beside it pointing toward the center. At the south is a downward-curving arc, like a single Binding curve, with two long legs ending in small outward feet and two shorter lines hanging from the arc between them.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element, so this is a fire spell. Its moderate size relative to the ring points to a moderate intensity. Regions signs that all point inward keep the magic inside the bounds of the ring. Columns signs in normal orientation, with the short crossbar outward, raise the magic in columns, and having several of them adds range and force. The mirrored curling glyphs are a guess as the Sign of Wind, which would add a wind-related, possibly spiraling, quality. The north zigzag is a guess as an enlarged Crushing sign fused with Columns, which would break the flame into smaller parts. The south glyph is a guess as a Binding-like arc with rays similar to Aeriforms Defined, which would hold those parts together. The seal is mirror-symmetric, so the two halves act evenly and no single direction is favored.
effect: The effect is tentative because several glyphs are guesses. It reads as a fire spell that raises flames in columns contained within the ring, likely given a swirling, wind-driven motion and broken into smaller flames held together above the seal.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed, with a wind sigil at the center, moderate in size relative to the ring. A curved caret matching the Launch sign sits at the north point with its apex toward the ring, and a second Launch sign mirrors it at the south point, also pointing outward. Three Levitation signs fan out along the west side and three along the east side, six in total, each with its arrow pointing inward toward the sigil. Four Stability and Level Planes signs, drawn as paired wavy lines, sit at the four intercardinal points.
justification: The wind sigil sets the element as the movement of air, at moderate intensity given its size. Levitation floats the target, and its six inward-pointing signs are balanced east and west, so the lift should hold steady rather than pull to one side. Stability and Level Planes keeps the target balanced on a level plane while still letting it move. Launch, a directional sign, drives the magic outward in a strong but short burst toward where it points. The two Launch signs point opposite ways, north and south, so the burst likely runs along that axis in both directions.
effect: Likely a wind spell that lifts the target into the air and holds it level, with short, strong bursts of air thrown out along the north–south axis. This reading comes from the sign combination alone, since the exact behavior of this seal is not established.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. Near the north point sits a single Envelopment sign: a tall vertical stroke with a diagonal hook at the top right and another at the bottom left. On either side of it, at the northwest and northeast, is an hourglass-like sign made of two triangles meeting at a point, closest to Reflection. The two are tilted and mirror each other. The center of the seal is empty. The lower half holds a large, irregular five-sided polygon with straight lines running outward from each of its corners. Three of these lines carry short crossbars, at the upper left, the right, and the lower left, so they read like Columns strokes. No standard element sigil is present.
justification: Envelopment makes the effect surround what it targets. The paired hourglass signs are read as Reflection, which works on a reflected image, though this match is a guess because they are tilted. The lower polygon matches no known sigil or sign. Its closest match is the Light sigil, a four-sided figure with lines extending from its corners, so this reading is also a guess. Taking it as a light-type sigil, the Columns-like crossbars would send the magic out in set directions. Together, light that wraps around a target and draws on reflection suggests an illusion or concealment effect.
effect: No confirmed function is known for this seal. Under the guessed reading, it would wrap a target in light shaped by reflected images, possibly concealing or disguising it.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. The center holds one large decorative sigil showing a four-legged animal with branching antlers. A triangular head sits at the left, the body runs horizontally, the legs angle downward, and a curled tail rises at the right. There is no element sigil. A Gathering sign sits at the north point and another at the south point, both with their arrowheads pointing inward toward the center. Four Diamond signs, one at each intercardinal point, are angled around the center. Two-line Stability and Level Planes signs sit at the east and west points.
justification: Without an element sigil, the decorative sigil sets the spell's subject. Its antlered quadruped form is closest to Torchstag, though that match is a guess. A decorative sigil gives the magic the rough shape of the creature it depicts, or limits the effect to that creature's physical counterpart. The two inward-pointing Gathering signs actively draw surrounding material in to build the effect. The four Diamond signs likely confine the effect to what lies within the object the seal is drawn on, leaving the object itself untouched. Stability and Level Planes is non-directional and keeps its target balanced in a level plane, so having it on both sides points to a steady, floating result.
effect: No established function is known for this exact seal. Read from its glyphs, it likely draws in nearby material and shapes it into a stag-like form that stays balanced and level. The Diamond signs would keep the effect contained without changing the object the seal is drawn on.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring closed. A large water sigil sits at the center, filling much of the inner space. Eight Columns signs are evenly spaced around it at the four cardinal and four intercardinal points, each with its crossbar against the ring and its stem pointing toward the center. Between each pair of Columns signs sits an open chevron matching the Regions sign, eight in total, all with their points aimed inward at the sigil. Nothing is cut off or hidden.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and its large size relative to the ring makes the effect strong. Columns is directional and shapes the magic into a column, and the number of Columns signs sets its range or quantity. Because the eight signs are spaced evenly with equal length, no direction is favored, so the column rises straight up from the seal rather than leaning to one side. All eight Regions signs point inward, which confines the magic to the space inside the ring and keeps it from appearing outside. The seal is radially symmetric, so every modifier reinforces the same centered, upward effect.
effect: Likely produces a strong, upright column of water confined to the area within the ring and rising straight up from the seal. No other signs are present to shape, harden, or direct it elsewhere.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A vertical stem runs top to bottom, capped at both ends by a horizontal bar whose ends turn back inward like brackets. Two nested upward-pointing chevrons sit on the stem's middle.
justification: This matches no known sign exactly. The stem with nested chevrons is closest to Gathering, so this is a guess, and the bracketed caps loosely resemble Projection mirrored top and bottom, suggesting the gathering is confined between two bounds.
effect: A spell component, read here as a Gathering variant, that draws surrounding material in for the spell to use, likely held within a bounded area. This reading is a guess.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single bird-shaped glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. A vertical stroke with a hooked flag at the top forms a head, two angled wings spread east and west with three short feather strokes each, and a separate tail below is drawn as an upward-pointing arrowhead on a vertical stem.
justification: The figure matches none of the standard modifier signs. Its clear bird outline is closest to a Bird decorative sigil, so that reading is a guess. A decorative glyph gives a spell the rough shape of the creature it depicts, and with no ring or elemental sigil here it is only a component.
effect: A spell component that, read as a Bird decorative sigil, would shape a spell's magic into a rough bird form, or limit its effect to birds.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. It forms a creature-like figure. At the top is a circle with a short vertical stroke inside it and two short horn-like strokes rising from its upper edge, like ear tufts. Two long wing-like arms extend from below the circle to either side, and each ends in an upturned stem with three short horizontal prongs. Below the circle, two crossing arcs meet in a downward V. Each arc ends in a forked, barbed tip that points outward and down. Beneath this, set apart from the figure, is a vertical stroke with two diagonal lines branching down from its middle, like an upward-pointing arrowhead on a stem.
justification: The figure matches no element sigil and no standard sign. Its round head with ear tufts, spread wings and talon-like tips read as a decorative sigil depicting an owl-like creature, most likely the Owlcat. This reading is a guess. Decorative sigils give magic the rough shape of the creature they depict. They can also target other spells shaped by the same sigil, or limit an effect to the physical counterpart of the design. The separate mark at the bottom is closest to a single-chevron Gathering sign or a stemmed Launch sign, which is also a guess. Read as Gathering, it would draw material in to build the shape. Read as Launch, it would send the shaped magic out in a short upward burst. Without a ring or an element sigil, the glyph cannot act on its own.
effect: This is a spell component rather than a full seal. As a decorative sigil, it would sculpt a spell's magic into the rough shape of an owl-like creature, or limit the spell to affecting that creature. Which element would be shaped cannot be determined from the image.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. It has a small open triangle on the left, an angular zigzag line ending in a diagonal stroke with three parallel ticks like a comb at the upper right, a large curved arc below, and two short separate diagonal dashes at the bottom.
justification: This glyph matches no listed sign. As a guess, it is closest to a decorative sigil of a bird: the triangle reads as a beak, the comb as wing feathers, the arc as a body, and the dashes as legs. Read that way, it shapes magic rather than setting an element.
effect: A spell component. If read as a bird decorative sigil, it sculpts a spell's magic into the rough shape of a bird and can limit the spell's effect to birds.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single asymmetric glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A line spirals inward about one and a half turns and ends in a small triangle near the center, while its outer end trails off at the bottom right into a short wavy tail.
justification: The glyph matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the asymmetric curl is closest to the Sign of Wind, also called Spiraling Wind, and the small triangle at its inner end resembles a Convergence mark pointing along the spiral; asymmetric signs behave unpredictably, so this reading is tentative.
effect: A spell component; read as a variant of the Sign of Wind, it likely adds a wind-related spiraling motion to a seal, possibly drawn in toward a single point, though its exact modifier effect is unclear.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single unidentified symbol on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A vertical stem carries a downward-pointing triangle at its top with two short ticks above it, an upward-opening arc with branched, talon-like tips at both ends, a downward-opening arch below that, and a bottom end that curls into a hook.
justification: This is one symbol, not a seal, so it has no element of its own. Its stacked arcs on a single stem with a curled end most closely resemble the Mimicry sign, and the triangle near the top echoes Convergence, but both readings are guesses.
effect: A spell component. If read as a Mimicry variant, it would make the spell's magic guide or imitate the movements of a target, possibly focused toward a single point.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. A large arc open at the bottom sits at the top, holding four short diagonal dashes. Below it, a vertical stroke rises from the lower left and curves up into a second, lower arc that sweeps right and down. A small triangle points left beside the vertical stroke. Two pairs of short parallel horizontal dashes sit beneath the figure, one pair under each end. Together the strokes form a rounded, bird-like figure with a head, body, beak and feet.
justification: The glyph matches no listed sign or element sigil. It reads as a figure drawn after a creature, so the closest match is a bird decorative sigil; this identification is a guess. The left-pointing triangle looks like a Convergence sign, but it reads as the beak of the drawing rather than a separate modifier. Decorative sigils give a spell's magic the rough shape of the creature they depict. They can also target other spells shaped by the same sigil, or limit a spell to that creature's physical counterpart. With no ring and no element sigil, this glyph cannot act on its own.
effect: A spell component, read here as a bird decorative sigil (a guess). Placed in a seal, it would give the spell's magic the rough shape of a bird, or limit the spell's effect to birds.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible eye-shaped glyph on a clean background: a large circle crossed by a symmetric curve that bows downward through it and extends past each side as straight diagonal lines rising up and outward, with a small closed inner circle and a solid dot at the center. No element sigil and no separate seal ring surround it.
justification: This matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Repetition, which shares the outer circle, the central dot, and a line crossing the circle that extends beyond it on both sides, though here the crossing line is a symmetric curve and the inner arc is closed into a circle. Reading it as a Repetition variant is a guess. On that reading it is a sign that can sit at the center of a seal in place of a sigil, so alone it acts as a modifier rather than a full spell.
effect: A spell component which, read as a Repetition variant, continuously resets affected objects to the state they had when the spell first took hold, restoring their shape and temperature if they change.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible sign on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A straight horizontal bar runs across the top. A vertical stem drops from the bar's midpoint and extends well below. Two curved lines hang from the ends of the bar and meet the stem at about mid-height, forming a cup or shield shape.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal. It matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Glaives: a central stem with two curved side prongs meeting it, here with the prong tips closed off by a top bar. This reading is a guess. Read as a Glaives variant, it would set how deeply a spell's magic embeds itself.
effect: A spell component. Read as a Glaives variant, it determines how deeply the spell's magic embeds itself into flesh.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph on a clean background with no ring: a long vertical line crossed low by a wide upward-opening V whose arm tips hook downward, with one dot on each side above the V. It matches no known sign or sigil exactly.
justification: The paired dots flanking a V meeting on a central stem most closely resemble the Earth sigil, so as a guess this is an earth-family variant sigil acting on solid matter. With no ring and no signs around it, nothing sets how that magic behaves.
effect: Its exact function is unknown; read as an Earth sigil variant, it would tentatively let a spell manipulate solid substances such as stone, sand, wood, or soil.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible sign on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. It is a long vertical line crossed at its midpoint by a V-shaped chevron whose arms angle upward, forming a downward-pointing arrowhead in the middle of the shaft.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal, so there is no element for it to act on. It matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Pulling, which is also a downward arrow on a vertical shaft but ends in a triangle. Reading it as a Pulling variant is a guess. Like Pulling, it would be a directional sign whose arrowhead sets which way the effect acts.
effect: A spell component. Read as a Pulling variant, it would pull the target toward the seal when the arrowhead points inward, and likely push it away when inverted.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A long vertical stroke runs from top to bottom. A wide U-shaped curve crosses it just below the middle, and its two arms sweep up and flare outward to either side, forming a psi-like or trident-like shape. The glyph is fully visible.
justification: This is one lone glyph, not a seal. It matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the closest is Glaives, which has the same trident form of a central vertical stroke flanked by two upward prongs, though here the prongs are a single smooth flaring curve rather than straight lines. With no sigil there is no element to act on, so read as Glaives it would only modify a spell.
effect: A spell component that, if read as Glaives, sets how deeply the spell's magic embeds itself into flesh. Glaives may sit outside the ring as long as they stay connected to it.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. An upright oval encloses two stacked circles that touch at the middle. A long hooked curve sweeps from a curl at the upper left down and around to join the bottom of the oval, and a matching curve rises from the top of the oval, arcs over to the right, and curls back at the lower right, making the glyph symmetric under a half turn.
justification: The glyph matches no known sign. As a guess, the closest is Solidification, whose two linked circles echo the stacked circles here, while the sweeping hooked curves resemble the S-strokes of the wind sigil. Because it has half-turn symmetry but no mirror symmetry, it would likely act as a non-directional sign that cannot be inverted.
effect: A spell component of unknown function. If it is read as a Solidification variant, which is only a guess, it would make the magic of its seal firmer and more solid.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph, fully visible on a clean background, with no ring around it. It is a square with a diamond inscribed inside it, each point of the diamond touching the midpoint of one side of the square, and a single dot at the center. No lines extend outward from the square or the diamond, and no other signs are present.
justification: This glyph matches no known sign or sigil exactly. The closest match is the Light sigil, which uses the same square-and-diamond figure but has four lines extending outward from the diamond's points. Here those lines are missing and a center dot is added. As a guess, this is a variant within the light branch of fire magic, with the changes altering how the light behaves. A secondary resemblance to the Diamond sign is possible, since the inner figure is a diamond. With no ring and no surrounding signs, nothing sets direction, shape, or behavior.
effect: The exact function of this symbol is unknown. On its own it is a component rather than a full spell. If it is read as a Light sigil variant, which is a guess, it would set a spell's element to light, creating and manipulating light that fades over time.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible symbol on a clean background: a square diamond standing on one point, crossed by two long parallel vertical lines that pass through its left and right sides and extend above and below it. No ring and no sigil.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal, and it matches no known sign exactly. The closest match is the Diamond sign, read here as a wider Diamond crossed by two lines; this is a guess, and the vertical lines may narrow or modify how it bounds the spell.
effect: A spell component. Read as a Diamond variant, it would limit a spell to objects inside the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph of two straight, parallel horizontal lines of equal length, one above the other, on a clean background. There is no ring and no sigil.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal, and it matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the closest is Stability and Level Planes, which is also built from parallel strokes, though those strokes are wavy rather than straight. Read that way, it is a non-directional modifier with no element of its own.
effect: A spell component. If read as Stability and Level Planes, it would keep the target balanced on a level plane in the air, free to move and rotate but staying level.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph on a clean background, made of two nested arches open at the bottom, a small arch inside a larger one, each with long straight legs. There is no ring and no sigil.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal. It matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Binding, which is also two stacked curves opening downward, so reading it as a taller form of Binding is a guess. With no sigil, it has no element to act on and only modifies a spell.
effect: Read as Binding, this is a spell component that halts the target material's movement and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring around it. At its core is a dome whose curved edge carries five triangular spikes. Above it, a short bar is topped by a tall upright triangle. Inside the dome, three dots form a triangle above a horizontal bar that spans the dome's base. On each side of the dome sits a small circle holding a triangle with a crossbar and a bar beneath it, with an open hook curling over its top. Below the dome hangs a spray of vertical bars of varying lengths and thicknesses, with a solid block at the center. One bar at the lower left ends in a small crossbar. No element sigil is present.
justification: The glyph as a whole matches no known sign or sigil, so each part is read against its closest sign, and each match is a guess. The spiked dome is closest to Rain, which summons a target material from above. The two side circles, each holding a crossbarred triangle, are closest to Strengthening, which hardens and reinforces. The tall triangle on top loosely resembles Launch, a short, powerful burst in the direction it points. The hanging bars are closest to Columns or Detection, suggesting the effect is cast downward in streaks. With no element sigil and no ring, nothing fixes what material is acted on, and the glyph cannot activate on its own.
effect: The function of this symbol is not known. Read tentatively from its closest signs, it would call something down from above in reinforced streaks, but no element or confirmed effect can be determined from the image.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single, fully visible symbol on a clean background. It is a horizontal band with a central bow made of two looped lobes, split by a short vertical stroke over a lower arc, and an inward-curling spiral at each end. There is no ring and no sigil.
justification: This is a lone symbol, not a seal, and it matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Pointing, which also has curls at both ends around a central figure, but that reading is a guess. As a non-directional sign it would shape the spell's material rather than set its element or direction.
effect: This is a spell component. Read as Pointing, it makes the target material form a cone that signs such as Columns can then direct.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. Three curved strokes branch at the top like antlers or talons and join a long S-curving central stroke. Two bent limbs extend from the middle and two longer limbs extend from the base, each ending in a short horizontal tick, so the glyph resembles a four-legged figure in mid-stride.
justification: The glyph matches no known sign. As a guess, its closest reading is a decorative sigil depicting an antlered, four-legged beast, similar in spirit to a stag-like decorative design. Decorative glyphs shape a spell's magic into the rough form of the creature they depict, but they carry no element, so this glyph only modifies a seal's form.
effect: A spell component of unknown function. Under the guessed decorative reading, it would sculpt a seal's magic into the rough shape of an antlered four-legged creature, and it would need an element sigil in the seal to produce any magic.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. A downward-pointing triangle sits at the top. A curved line passes behind and through it, forming an open loop around the triangle's lower point and then sweeping down into a small inward curl at the bottom.
justification: This glyph matches no known sign exactly, so any reading is a guess. The inverted triangle is closest to Convergence, which focuses a spell's magic down to a single point and can pack loose particles tightly together. The looping line with a curled tail is closest to the Wind sign, or possibly the Purification sign; reading it as Wind adds an air-related, spiraling quality. On this reading the glyph would act as a compound modifier that draws magic into one point while giving it a whirling motion. Because it has no ring and no sigil, it is a component rather than a working seal.
effect: A spell component whose exact function is unknown. Read as Convergence combined with a Wind-like curl, it would likely focus a spell's magic toward a single point while giving it a spiraling, wind-like motion.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring. It is a square with a diamond inscribed inside it, a short straight line extending outward from each diamond point at north, east, south and west, a short diagonal line extending outward from each of the four square corners, and a dot at the center.
justification: The square, inscribed diamond and four cardinal lines match the Light sigil, while the four diagonal corner lines and the center dot are extra marks not found on it. The closest match is therefore the Light sigil, and reading this as a variant of it is a guess. Standing alone without a ring or signs, it only sets the element of a spell.
effect: A spell component, read as a light-domain sigil that creates and manipulates light, which fades over time. How the extra corner rays and center dot change that light is unknown.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring around it. It is a square with a short straight line extending outward from the middle of each side, pointing north, east, south, and west. Inside the square sits a smaller diamond whose points face the four cardinal directions but do not touch the square. Four diagonal strokes cross the diamond's edges, one toward each corner of the square, forming an X that passes behind the diamond. No other signs are present.
justification: The glyph matches no known sign or sigil exactly. The closest match is the Light sigil, which also combines a square, an inner diamond, and four cardinal strokes. Reading it as a Light sigil variant is a guess. Here the diamond is detached from the square and the added diagonal X sets it apart, which suggests a sigil in the fire and light domain with an altered behavior. Because this is a lone sigil with no surrounding ring or modifier signs, it only sets the kind of magic and does not direct it.
effect: A spell component, read tentatively as a variant of the Light sigil, so it would set a seal to create and manipulate light. The way its added diagonal strokes change that light cannot be determined from the image.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph, fully visible on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. A circle sits at the top on a vertical stem. An upward-opening arc crosses the stem partway down, and a downward-opening arc meets it at the same point below.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal, so there is no element for it to act on. It matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the closest is Dispersion, which also pairs a stem with an upward curve; the circle on top and the extra lower arc would be variations on that reading.
effect: A spell component. Read as a Dispersion variant, it would make the seal's magic pour or spread outward rather than beam in one direction, but this effect is uncertain.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible symbol on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. Eight hooked, square-cornered arms overlap in a pinwheel around a central square, and inside that square sits a diamond enclosing a smaller diamond.
justification: This glyph matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the nested diamonds at the center are closest to the Diamond sign, and the bracket-like arms loosely recall Expansion's corners. The pinwheel has rotational symmetry but no mirror symmetry, which fits a non-directional sign that cannot be inverted.
effect: This is a spell component, not a full spell. Read as a Diamond variant, which is a guess, it would limit a spell to the contents of the container it is drawn on without affecting the container itself.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A long vertical line runs through the center, with one dot on each side of it. Beyond each dot, a chevron points inward toward the line: one on the west side and one on the east side, mirroring each other.
justification: This glyph matches no known sign exactly. The closest match is Cooling, which also places dots on either side of a central vertical line, though here there is one dot per side instead of a pair. The two outer chevrons resemble Regions signs pointing inward, and inward-pointing Regions confine magic to the area within them. Reading it as a Cooling-like core flanked by inward Regions is a guess. On that reading, it is a cooling modifier whose effect is drawn toward and held at the central line.
effect: A spell component, not a full seal. If the guessed reading is right, it would cool the target and keep that cooling confined to the space between the chevrons. Without a sigil or ring, it only modifies a spell.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single plain cross on a clean background, made of one vertical and one horizontal line of equal length crossing at the center with no gap. There is no ring and no sigil.
justification: This is one sign, not a seal, and it matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Crosshair, which has a gap at the center and shorter ends, so this reading is a guess. Read as Crosshair with all four arms equal, it gives no single preferred direction.
effect: A spell component. Read as Crosshair, it would make the seal's magic target whatever its arms point at, here evenly in all four directions.

name: Unknown Magic
