description: A single glyph on a clean background with no ring and no sigil. A rounded arch stands on two straight vertical legs, and a horizontal line crosses both legs and runs past them on each side, ending in a small open circle at the east and west ends.
justification: This glyph matches no known sign. As a guess, the closest is Solidification, because both have two open circles joined by a straight line, here running horizontally through an arch that loosely resembles Stretch. Read as a Solidification variant, it would act as a modifier that makes the magic tied to it more solid, with the arch possibly marking the shape or span that hardens.
effect: A spell component, not a full spell. Read as a Solidification variant, which is a guess, it would make the magic connected to it more solid, likely within an arched form.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A fully visible arrangement of signs on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil, leaving the center empty. Four half-disc signs, each a semicircular curve closed by a straight line, sit at the north, east, south, and west points. They are rotated in a pinwheel: the north one has its flat side facing east, the east one faces south, the south one faces west, and the west one faces north. Four identical X-shaped marks sit at the four intercardinal points.
justification: No sigil is present, so no element is set and the arrangement only modifies a spell. The half-discs match no known sign; the closest is Binding, whose curved arc they resemble, so reading them as Binding is a guess. The X marks are closest to Collection without its closing bar, which is also a guess. Each half-disc is turned a quarter step from the last, a clockwise rotation like angled Pulling signs. Read this way, the arrangement would bind gathered material together and set it turning around the center.
effect: The function of this glyph is unknown. It is a spell component with no sigil. On the guessed reading it would collect nearby material, bind it into a single unit, and give it a rotating motion around the seal's center, but this is tentative.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no other signs. It is an upward-pointing triangle with three circles, each straddling one edge: one on the upper left side, one on the upper right side, and one on the base. From each circle a straight line extends outward, toward the northwest, the east, and the south-southwest.
justification: The glyph matches no known sign. The closest match is the Fire sigil, which is also an upward triangle with three short rays at the upper left, upper right, and bottom, so this reading is a guess. Here each ray starts from a circle sitting on the triangle's edge, which suggests a variant derived from the Fire sigil in the way Light is. On that reading it sets a fire-domain element, with the circles adding some unidentified quality to the flame or heat.
effect: A lone glyph and a likely sigil-level component rather than a working spell. Read as a Fire-derived variant, it would produce some form of flame or heat, but its specific function is not known.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no other signs. It is an upward-pointing triangle whose sides cross at each corner to form a teardrop loop, and a small open circle sits just beyond each loop at the north, southwest, and southeast points.
justification: The glyph matches no known sign or sigil exactly. Its closest match is the Fire sigil, which is also an upward triangle with marks radiating from it, so this reading is a guess. On that reading, the looped corners and outer circles would be variant modifiers on a fire-domain sigil, much as Light is a variant drawn close to Fire. Standing alone without a ring, it is a component rather than a working seal.
effect: Its exact function is unknown. If it is read as a variant of the Fire sigil, it would act as a spell component that sets the spell to create or manipulate flames or heat, with the loops and circles altering that effect in an unknown way.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single composite glyph, fully visible on a clean background, with no ring and no element sigil. At the center are two triangles stacked tip to tip in an hourglass shape, separated by a small gap at their points. A chevron sits at the east and another at the west, each with its point aimed inward at the hourglass. Four single-line right-angle corner brackets frame the whole glyph, one at each intercardinal point, with their corners pointing outward.
justification: No known sign matches this glyph as a whole, so it is read as a cluster of familiar shapes, and each reading is a guess. The central hourglass is closest to Reflection, which targets a reflected image. The two inward-pointing chevrons are closest to Regions signs pointing inward, which confine magic to the space inside them. The outward-facing corner brackets are closest to a simplified Expansion sign; Expansion is semi-directional and grows its target when its corners point outward. Read together, the glyph would target a reflected image, confine it to the framed area, and enlarge it there. There is no sigil and no ring, so it sets no element and cannot act alone.
effect: A spell component, not a working seal. Under the guessed reading, it would draw on a reflected image, hold it within the bounds the glyph marks, and enlarge it. Its exact behavior inside a full seal is unknown.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no other signs. It is a plain S-shaped stroke without curled ends, flanked by four short dashes on each side. The middle two dashes are horizontal and the outer two angle slightly away from the S.
justification: The closest match is the Wind sigil, which is an S flanked by short dashes, but this S lacks the spiral ends and has four dashes per side instead of three. Reading it as a Wind sigil or a close wind-domain variant is a guess. With no ring and no signs, it sets only the element and not how the magic behaves.
effect: A lone sigil, so it is a component rather than a working spell. Read as a wind-type sigil, it would make a seal move and manipulate air rather than create it.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. It is a tall diamond with a dot at its center, and a horizontal bar runs across its top point.
justification: This glyph matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the closest is the Diamond sign, which shares the rhombus shape; the top bar and central dot are extra marks that may modify it, and the bar loosely echoes the crossbar of Columns. Read as a Diamond variant, it is a lone sign and would only modify a spell's sigil.
effect: A spell component. Read as a Diamond variant, it would make a spell act only on what lies inside the container it is drawn on, leaving the container itself unaffected.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single glyph of three straight, parallel horizontal lines of equal length, evenly spaced, on a clean background. There is no ring and no sigil.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal, and it matches no known sign exactly. As a guess, the closest is the three-lined Stability and Level Planes sign, drawn with straight rather than wavy strokes, so it would act as a non-directional modifier that behaves the same however it is turned.
effect: A spell component. If read as Stability and Level Planes, it would balance the target on a level plane in the air, letting it turn and drift while staying level; this reading is a guess.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single plain arrow sign on a clean background, a long vertical stroke topped by an open chevron pointing up, with no crossbar at its base. No sigil and no ring.
justification: This matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Levitation, which has the same upward arrow but adds a bar at the foot, so reading it as a Levitation variant is a guess; as a lone sign with no sigil, it can only modify a spell.
effect: A spell component that, read as Levitation, floats the target into the air, with the length of the arrow setting how far, how fast, or how much weight it carries.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single eight-spoked star of four straight lines crossing at one center point, on a clean background. There is no ring and no sigil.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal. It matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Concealment, which shares the same eight-spoke star but adds eye-shaped marks at four of the tips, so reading it as a bare form of Concealment is a guess.
effect: A spell component. Read as a form of Concealment, it would hide the target object.

name: Unknown Magic
description: A single fully visible glyph on a clean background, with no ring and no sigil. A straight horizontal baseline runs across the bottom. Two concentric semicircular arcs rise from it, a large outer arch and a smaller inner arch, joined into one band like an arched doorway or bridge span. The baseline extends beyond both sides of the arch.
justification: This is a lone sign, not a seal. It matches no known sign exactly. The closest is Binding, which also stacks a larger arc over a smaller one, though here the arcs are joined to each other and set on a baseline. Reading it as a Binding variant is a guess. On that reading, the sign would act on whatever material a sigil supplies, holding it together. With no sigil present, it only modifies a spell.
effect: A spell component. If read as a variant of Binding, which is a guess, it halts the movement of the target material and binds it together so it acts and moves as a single unit.

name: Wall Bend
description: A manga panel showing a round seal drawn on a flat surface, seen at a steep angle so it appears as a flattened oval. A hand or tool reaches in at the upper left, and the panel frame cuts off the lower and right edges, so the seal is only partly visible. Whether the ring is open or closed cannot be confirmed. Inside, several arrow-shaped marks point toward the lower right and resemble Pulling signs. A small looping mark sits left of center, and a few smaller strokes are scattered nearby. At this size and angle, no element sigil can be clearly identified.
justification: The arrow-shaped marks match the Pulling sign, a directional sign that draws the target toward the seal, and angling it adds a twisting pull. Their shared slant suggests the pull runs in one direction relative to the seal. The central glyph is too small and distorted to confirm as an earth sigil, and the remaining strokes cannot be matched to known signs, so the element and any further modifiers are not readable here.
effect: Likely pulls earthen materials such as stone, soil and brickwork in a set direction relative to the seal, bending them out of shape. This assumes the unreadable central glyph is an earth sigil and that the hidden part of the seal matches the visible Pulling signs.

name: Warmth-Retention Seal
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black ink on a plain background, with the outer ring closed. A small fire sigil sits at the center inside its own closed inner circle. Four straight lines run from the inner circle to the outer ring at the north, south, east and west points. Each line splits into a Y-shaped fork just before the ring, so the fork and the ring enclose a small triangle. At the four intercardinal points sit L-shaped corner marks that box off a small square against the ring, with each corner's vertex pointing inward toward the center. No other signs are present.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as heat. Its small size relative to the ring sets a low intensity. The inner circle, spokes and corner marks form one surrounding structure that matches no known sign; the same pattern also appears in the Time Stop spell. As a guess, the forked spokes are closest to Regions signs pointing inward on a stem, which would keep the magic within the ring. Also as a guess, the inward-pointing corners are closest to an inverted Expansion sign, which reduces rather than grows. Read together, the structure would hold a weak fire effect inside the seal's bounds and keep it from building, giving gentle, contained, constant heat. This fits the shared pattern with Time Stop, which suggests holding a state steady.
effect: Maintains a steady, low heat on whatever the seal is used on.

name: Warmth-Retention Seal
description: A manga panel of a round-bellied pot resting in a stand, with an inset diagram of a fully visible seal, ring closed. A small fire sigil sits at the center inside its own small inner circle. Four straight lines run diagonally from the inner circle out to the ring, dividing the space into four sections. At the north, east, south and west points sit four matching inward-pointing shapes, each a pointed chevron closed off toward the ring, so the whole surround forms one symmetric figure. An arrow points to a ring on the pot stand where the seal is applied, but no glyph is legible there.
justification: The fire sigil sets the element as heat, and its small size relative to the ring keeps the intensity low. The surrounding figure matches no known sign. The closest reading, offered as a guess, is four Regions signs pointing inward. All Regions signs pointing inward confine the magic to the area inside the ring, so the heat would stay on whatever sits within the seal instead of spreading outward. The diagonal lines tying the inner circle to the ring add no known modifier under this reading. A small, contained fire sigil with no Columns or other directional signs gives a gentle heat that stays put.
effect: Keeps whatever it is used on at a steady, low heat.

name: Water Horse Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A water sigil sits at the center. Directly above it is a large angular figure shaped like a horse, with a short dash under each leg. In the upper west and upper east sit two Columns signs turned on their sides, each with its stem pointing inward toward the horse, so they face opposite directions. A Mimicry sign stands vertically on each side of the water sigil, at the west and east. Below the water sigil is an alternating row of five marks: three single straight strokes (leaning left, near vertical, leaning right) and, between them, two Regions-like chevrons, one upright and one tilted.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, and the horse figure is a decorative sigil that gives the water a horse's rough shape. The Mimicry signs guide the shaped water to imitate the movements of what the decorative sigil depicts. The paired Columns signs push magic in opposing directions around the horse, holding its form in place rather than sending it off in one direction. The two chevrons match Regions, which sets where the magic manifests in relation to the seal. The three straight strokes match no known sign. The closest is a single stroke of Aeriforms Defined, though this is a guess. On that reading they would work with the Regions signs to shape where the water forms beneath the figure.
effect: Creates water shaped like a horse that moves like a real horse and can be mounted, guided, and controlled by its caster. The ring is open, and the spell activates only once the ring is closed.

name: Beast Repellent
description: A hand-drawn seal with the ring closed and the left edge of the ring meeting the panel border. A large unidentified sigil sits at the center: a vertical stem topped by a horizontal bar, with angled branches along the stem and hooked strokes at its base. A light sigil, a square crossed by a diamond with spokes, sits at the east point and another at the west point. Small round, star-like glyphs mark the north and south points. Four Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points between the light sigils and the north and south glyphs, with the short bars facing outward.
justification: The two light sigils set the seal's element as light. The central sigil matches no known sigil. Its top bar and downward stem are closest to the earth sigil, so reading it as an earth variant is a guess. On that reading, it would anchor or ground the light rather than add a second element. Four balanced Columns signs send the magic out as columns, with no single favored direction, so the light radiates evenly around the seal. The small north and south glyphs match no known sign. They likely narrow what the light acts on, but their exact role cannot be read.
effect: Produces light that radiates outward from the seal and repels animals from the area around it.

name: Crystal Ribbon
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, ring open at the bottom. A single large Stretch sign arcs around the center, with its open side facing south and its two short feet angled outward toward the lower ring. At the center sits a lattice glyph of two sets of three parallel diagonal lines crossing to form a small diamond grid. It does not match the fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigils. No other signs are present.
justification: The central lattice glyph is read as a crystal variant sigil. This is a guess based on its faceted, crystalline grid shape, and it would set the magic to crystal. Stretch is meant to surround the central sigil, which it does here, and it draws affected material out into long, flexible ribbons. Together, a crystal sigil enclosed by Stretch yields crystal formed into a flexible ribbon. Because the ring is open, the seal would not activate until the gap is closed.
effect: Creates a soft, flexible ribbon made of crystal.

name: Forbidden Flames
description: A manga panel showing a seal drawn on a flat surface and seen at an angle, so the ring appears as an ellipse. The ring is closed and the seal is fully visible, with billowing smoke rising just above its upper edge. At the center is a short vertical stroke with a dot on each side, flanked by two chevrons pointing inward toward it. Four circled glyphs sit at the cardinal points. The north, east and west ones are circles crossed by a slanted stroke, and the south one is a circle holding an A-like triangle with a crossbar. Four T-shaped Columns signs sit at the intercardinal points, one between each pair of circled glyphs. The glyphs are small, but every one can be made out.
justification: The central glyph matches no known element sigil. Its closest known match is the Cooling sign, a bar between dots, framed by chevrons resembling Regions signs pointing inward; this is a guess. Regions pointing inward limit the magic to the space inside the ring. The four Columns signs are evenly spaced and balanced, so they send the effect straight up in a column above the seal. The circled glyphs are closest to the Orb sign; the southern one may instead be a Strengthening sign set inside a circle, also a guess. Read this way, Orb gathers the produced material in a rounded space above the seal, and the Columns push it upward. Under that reading the seal makes its effect inside the ring and drives it upward. The Cooling-like center is unexpected for a flame spell, so the element cannot be confirmed from the glyph alone.
effect: Creates a small fire that burns like an ordinary fire spell. It is unknown whether it has any additional or unusual properties.

name: Forbidden Glow
description: A small manga panel showing a round sheet with a seal on it and a hand holding a pen at the right edge. The ring is fully visible and appears closed. About eight small T-shaped marks are spaced evenly around the inside of the ring. They match Columns signs, though at this size their orientation is hard to judge. A small mark sits at the center, but it is too tiny and rough to identify as any known sigil.
justification: The ring of evenly spaced Columns signs is balanced, so the magic would rise as a column above the seal rather than leaning to one side. The central sigil, which would set the element, cannot be read, so the type of magic cannot be confirmed from the visible strokes.
effect: The element cannot be determined from the image because the central sigil is unreadable. The spell is known to create a brief display of glowing, flickering sparkles of light, which the balanced ring of Columns signs would send upward from the seal.

name: Illusory Labyrinth
description: A fully visible seal drawn in black ink on a plain background, ring closed. It has a triple border: an outer band filled with a row of small triangles, a middle band with looping knot-like ornaments at regular intervals, and an inner ring. Just inside the inner ring, a continuous band of small chevrons resembling Regions signs runs around the whole circumference, with the chevrons pointing along the ring rather than inward or outward. Inside that band, roughly twenty Columns signs are spread radially around the seal. The center holds a large unidentified sigil: a dome shape with three dots, short spikes along its rim, and a fringe of heavy black bars hanging below it. On either side of this dome sits a small circle containing a triangle with a crossbar, resembling a Strengthening sign. Above the dome are a tall narrow triangle at north and two filled triangles at northeast and northwest. At the four intercardinal points sit branching, antler-like glyphs. At east, west and south are smaller marks that combine a triangle or V shape with a curl, the southern one resembling a Wind or Purification sign beneath a V.
justification: The central sigil matches none of the element sigils and is the same one used in a scalewolf curse, so it sets a non-elemental kind of magic. The many Columns signs project that magic outward and upward over a wide area, and having this many of them widens its range. The chevron band is read as Regions signs, which is a guess. Because they all point the same way around the ring, they would send the effect circling back on itself instead of out in one direction, which fits a space that loops. The circled triangles are read as Strengthening, also a guess, and would reinforce the effect. The antler-like glyphs are closest to Glaives or Entwining, another guess, and would bind the effect firmly to its target area. The curled marks at the cardinal points cannot be matched with confidence.
effect: Creates a vast underground labyrinth in which space is distorted and loops endlessly, so anyone who walks too far ends up back where they started and cannot escape.

name: Petrification
description:
A large, fully visible seal on a page, seen at a slight angle, with its outer ring closed. At the center sits an inner ring holding a sigil of overlapping rotated squares around a small square. A band of small repeated signs around it alternates marks that look like inverted Columns and inverted Dispersion with dots. Outside that band are four sections at the north, east, south and west. Each has a half-circle enclosing a branching, crossed glyph, three small inverted Dispersion-like signs beneath it, and a row of vertical strokes. The strokes are mostly hooked lines resembling Envelopment, with some topped by small circles. At the four intercardinal points between these sections sit fern-like branching glyphs with curled bases. Four smaller circles are set into the outer ring, each flanked by two small triangle signs that hold a spiral:
- one at the upper left holding a snowflake-like glyph with diamonds, close to Concealment
- one at the right holding a glyph resembling the water sigil
- one at the lower right holding four curls around a small circle
- one at the left holding a dotted circle ringed by triangles

The band of the outer ring carries small Columns-like signs paired with short triple dashes.
justification: The central overlapping-square sigil matches no element sigil exactly. Its closest match is the square-in-square form of the Light sigil, but that is a guess, and it may be a distinct variant. The inverted Columns and inverted Dispersion signs repeated around it push the magic outward horizontally in every direction rather than up in a beam, so the effect spreads over the surrounding area. The many Envelopment-like strokes make that effect wrap around and coat whatever it reaches. The fern-like branching glyphs most resemble Glaives, again a guess; read that way, they set how deeply the magic sinks into flesh, letting it act on living things as well as objects. The satellite circles add further sub-spells, including a water-like sigil and a Concealment-like glyph, whose exact roles cannot be isolated. Together these signs describe a spell that radiates outward, envelops everything around it and works into its substance.
effect: Turns everyone and everything nearby, living or inanimate, into a rock-like material.

name: Reverse Time
description: A manga panel. A seal drawn on a bare chest is revealed by hands pulling open a shirt. The ring is an oval with a thick dark band. Inside, a six-pointed star is built entirely from straight lines, layered with nested triangles and smaller geometric shapes, with a smaller star at its center. No element sigil is visible. Outside the ring, small branching, twig-like marks radiate from the top and bottom edges. The right hand overlaps the right edge of the ring and the shirt fabric covers part of the lower left, so it cannot be confirmed whether the ring is open or closed.
justification: There is no fire, water, earth, wind, or light sigil, so the spell's element is not set by an element glyph. The interlocking straight-line hexagram matches no listed sign. As a guess, it is closest in role to Repetition, the time glyph that can stand in the center in place of a sigil. Read that way, the star sets time as the domain of the spell, but it is drawn differently enough to act on time in a different way than Repetition. The branching marks outside the ring loosely resemble Gathering or Glaives, but they are too small and partly hidden to read with confidence.
effect: Reverses time on the target to undo wear and other damage, reaching back at most one day. The effect is temporary: when the time frame runs out, the glyph vanishes and the target returns to the state it would have been in without the spell. It can be reapplied to repeat the effect.

name: Scalewolf Curse
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background with its inner ring closed. Around the inner ring runs an outer band studded with small triangular points, with four larger points at north, east, south and west. The interior holds no recognizable element sigil. Near the top, three dots form a triangle beneath a large arch that opens downward. Below them a horizontal bar sits across the center, with four stems hanging from it, each ending in a downward-splayed fork.
justification: No fire, water, earth, wind or light sigil is present, so the three-dot triangle under the arch acts as the central keystone. The same three-dot keystone also appears in the illusory labyrinth seal, but its function on its own is unknown. The arch matches no known sign exactly. Its closest match is Stretch, which turns solid matter into long, flexible ribbons, so as a guess it reshapes the target's matter. The four forked stems are closest to the fork of Gathering, also a guess. Gathering lets a spell draw in material from its surroundings, and four of them would pull that material in strongly. Read together, the seal would gather nearby material and work it into the target's form. The spiked outer band is unidentified, and its points are evenly spaced, so it adds no direction.
effect: Permanently transforms the target's body by fusing it with material bound to it. A cloak containing scalewolf fur and scales, for example, merges with the wearer and turns them into a scalewolf.

name: Tracking Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a clean background, outer ring closed, with no element sigil. A long horizontal line crosses the center from edge to edge, overlaid by a zigzag line spanning the same width. Inside the outer ring are two partial inner arcs. One runs from the north around the west side and ends in a small two-stroke hooked mark. The other runs from the south around the east side and ends in a matching mark. Just above the center line, at north, sits a small circle with a stem rising from it. At south, a matching circle has a stem pointing down. In the northeast and southwest sits a diamond crossed by two curved strokes. In the northwest and southeast sits a starburst-like sign: a short vertical line crossed by several horizontal and diagonal strokes. The whole layout is point-symmetric, each sign mirrored by a copy rotated 180 degrees.
justification: No element sigil is present, so the center line and its signs carry the spell. None of the glyphs match a known sign exactly, so each reading below is a guess. The zigzag most resembles a stretched Crushing sign. The circle-and-stem glyphs resemble one half of a Solidification sign, which would fix magic onto a target. The diamond with curved strokes resembles a Diamond sign joined with Holding, which would limit the effect to the marked object and keep it held there. The starburst sign is closest to Concealment, which would keep the mark hidden. The hooked ends of the inner arcs are closest to Regions, which would extend the effect outward from the ring. Read together, these guesses describe a hidden, persistent mark that stays bound to one object while its presence can still be sensed from a distance. The 180-degree symmetry would keep the effect balanced.
effect: Marks a magical item so that it can be tracked afterward.

name: Floatglow Lamp Seal
description: A fully visible seal drawn on a textured, paper-like background. The ring appears closed, with its lowest arc running along the bottom edge of the image. A Sigil of Light sits at the center, small relative to the ring. Four Levitation signs sit at the north, east, south and west points, each with its arrowhead pointing inward toward the sigil. Four Convergence signs, drawn as small triangles, sit at the four intercardinal points.
justification: The light sigil makes this a light spell, and its small size means a modest intensity. Four Levitation signs evenly balanced around the center float the magic upward, and balanced Levitation shapes it into a sphere. The four Convergence signs focus the magic around a single point, keeping the light compact rather than spread out. Together they produce a contained, floating orb of light.
effect: Creates a small ball of light that floats above the seal.

name: Vapor Bubble Spell
description: A manga panel showing a seal with two concentric rings, both closed, with a strip of unrelated panel art along the left edge. A water sigil sits at the center inside the inner ring. Two Gathering signs cross the inner ring at the north and south points, their arrowheads pointing in toward the sigil. In the band between the rings, Columns signs sit at the north, northeast, northwest, southeast, southwest and south points, six in all, with their bars facing outward. Two wind sigils, drawn on their sides, sit at the east and west points. Four Cooling signs sit in the gaps beside the north and south Columns signs. The bottom edge of the image cuts through the south Columns sign and the lowest part of the outer ring, so they are only partly visible.
justification: The water sigil sets the element, so the spell acts on water. The second ring adds effects to that core. The two wind sigils move air, and the inward-pointing Gathering signs draw material in from the surroundings, so together they pull in moist air. The Cooling signs chill that air so its moisture condenses into water. The six Columns signs direct the magic upward from the seal. The hidden part of the south Columns sign is assumed to match the visible north one, since the rest of the seal is symmetric.
effect: Draws in moist air, cools it, and condenses the moisture into an orb of fresh water that is held above the seal.

name: Pegasus Carriage Spell
description: A fully visible seal on a printed page, with stray lettering at the top left and a panel corner at the bottom left. Two concentric rings, both closed, form an outer band filled with a continuous chain of curled Wind signs. Inside, the outer edge of the main area is lined with many small Columns signs pointing inward. A Stability and Level Planes sign (three wavy lines) sits at the center, with four small Columns signs around it facing inward. Four closed subseals sit at the north, south, east and west. The north and south subseals each hold a triangular sigil with three spiral arms, the Whorling Wind sigil, with Columns signs around it. The east and west subseals each hold an S-shaped sigil, the Wind Underfoot sigil, ringed by small marks that look like Levitation and Aeriforms Defined signs. Between the subseals are clusters of curled Wind signs and small angled Columns signs. The smallest marks are too fine to read individually.
justification: No single element sigil anchors the seal. Instead it is a compound of wind-type parts. Stability and Level Planes at the center keeps the target balanced on a level plane, and the inward Columns around it focus that effect. The Wind Underfoot subseals paired with Levitation and Aeriforms Defined support a solid object in the air and lift it. The Whorling Wind subseals with their Columns move air through rotation. The angled Columns between the subseals, all turned the same way, likely add a rotational push. The dense border of Columns adds force inward around the seal. The Wind signs in the outer band have no clearly known function beyond relating to wind.
effect: Makes the object it is drawn on fly while keeping it steady, level and upright, even while it is being pulled.

name: Bubble Carriage Seal
description: A printed seal with a double ring, cut off along the bottom edge of the frame. The visible part of the ring is unbroken, but the bottom is not shown. At the center is a wind-family sigil: an S-shaped spiral flanked east and west by fans of three lines converging toward the spiral, with four dots at the intercardinal points. This matches the Aeriforms variant rather than the plain wind sigil. Just inside the ring, a continuous band alternates Columns signs and Regions signs, with roughly twenty of each visible. The Columns signs sit with their crossbars toward the ring. The Regions chevrons all point outward toward the ring. The lowest part of the band is hidden by the frame edge.
justification: The Aeriforms sigil sets the element as wind magic that creates air rather than moving it. Regions signs pointing outward place the magic toward and beyond the ring rather than in the center. The many evenly spaced Columns signs around the whole circumference push equally in every direction, so the effect has no single heading and spreads into a rounded volume. Together they shape the generated air into an enclosing bubble. Because the band is evenly spaced, the hidden lower section is assumed to continue the same alternation, giving twenty-four of each sign.
effect: Creates a supply of breathable air shaped into a rough bubble that holds together underwater. This assumes the hidden bottom of the seal mirrors the visible top and that the ring is closed there.

name: Twinned Bottles
description: A round seal on a pale, textured background, cropped so that its bottom edge and part of its left side fall outside the frame. Where the ring is visible it appears closed, but the bottom stretch cannot be seen. At the center sits an hourglass glyph of two triangles joined by crossing lines, matching the Reflection sign. It is framed by four corner brackets matching the Expansion sign, with their corners at the outer positions. The two lower brackets are only partly visible. A short horizontal dash sits east of the center and another sits west. Around the inside of the ring, about seven or eight identical small glyphs are visible, each a curved base topped with small raised bumps like a crown. These match no known sign. Any further glyphs along the bottom are cut off.
justification: No element sigil is visible, so the Reflection-like hourglass takes the central place as a sign rather than a sigil. Reflection targets a mirrored image, and its two matched triangles suggest one thing mirroring another. The surrounding Expansion corners point outward, which normally makes a target grow. Here they may instead widen the reach of that mirroring, though this is a guess. The east and west dashes match no known sign. The crown-shaped ring glyphs are closest to Partition, also a guess. Read that way, they would outline the boundary of what the spell acts on, here the space inside a vessel. Taken together, the reading is a spell that keeps two bounded spaces mirroring each other over any distance. The bottom half is hidden, so it is assumed to mirror the visible top half.
effect: Links two separate vessels so that their contents always stay evenly split between them, no matter how far apart they are. The spell activates as liquid runs along the etched lines of the seal. This assumes the hidden lower part of the seal mirrors the visible upper part.

name: Capture Pennant Spell
description: A seal of two concentric rings, both closed, drawn on a page with some figure art at the left edge that does not cover the glyph. A Repetition sign fills the center of the inner ring, with a small circle wrapped by a curving S-shaped line that crosses the inner ring. Four Sights Set signs sit at the intercardinal points, each with its diamond on the outer ring and its arrow pointing inward to the inner ring. Entwining signs straddle the space between the rings at the four cardinal points. The east and west Entwining signs lie horizontally and each carries a Strengthening sign on its inner end. The north Entwining sign is drawn small and simple, and the south one sits upright between the rings.
justification: No element sigil is present. The central Repetition sign takes the sigil's place and makes this a time spell that keeps resetting the object to its original state, so it resists damage and bending. The four inward Sights Set signs let the caster aim the spell at a chosen target with their mind. The Entwining signs make the object the seal is drawn on wrap itself around that target. The Strengthening signs on the east and west Entwining signs make the object harder and more durable.
effect: Lets the caster pick a target with their mind and makes the object bearing the seal wrap tightly around it. The object is also reinforced and keeps resetting to its original state, so it resists damage and bending.
